title: Dimensional Collapse and Representation Entanglement: Context-Dependent Effects of Residual Connections in Over-Parameterized MLP Autoencoders
abstract: Residual connections have become a standard architectural component in deep learning, yet their effect on disentanglement in MLP autoencoders remains understudied. Recent work has shown that unsupervised disentanglement requires strong inductive biases, raising the question of whether common architectural choices can supply them. In this work, we investigate the failure modes of over-parameterized MLP autoencoders and test whether residual connections can mitigate them. We train small and large MLP autoencoders, with and without residual connections, on two datasets of varying complexity (dSprites and 3D Shapes), and evaluate them using MIG, DCI, and Effective Rank. Our experiments reveal two distinct failure modes: dimensional collapse on simple data, where the model converges to a shortcut solution using only a single latent dimension, and representation entanglement on complex data, where the model uses almost its full latent space but fails to separate the factors of variation. We find that residual connections partially mitigate dimensional collapse but are entirely ineffective against representation entanglement. These results suggest that architectural changes such as using residual connections alone are insufficient for disentanglement, and that an explicit disentanglement objective is likely required.

title: Operationalizing the QUETZAL Framework for Agent-Supported Instructional Design
abstract: This paper develops a conceptual architecture for the QUETZAL Agent, intended to support educators and instructional designers in transforming existing learning paths into adaptive learning offerings. Drawing on Paper2Agent and the Model Context Protocol, the design connects instructional decision logic, technical operationalization, and agentic interaction. An inspectable adaptation specification makes proposals, rationales, and responsibilities traceable. Human decision authority and iterative review are central design principles. A hypothetical use case illustrates the architecture; its practical effectiveness remains to be investigated empirically.

title: Going Faster: Privacy-Preserving Shortest Paths from Start to End
abstract: Finding shortest paths in graphs is a fundamental combinatorial optimization problem with numerous applications, e. g., in graph centrality measures, computational biology, and business process analysis. To address privacy constraints in such applications, Secure Multi-Party Computation (SMPC) protocols can compute the lengths of shortest paths on secret-shared graphs. Many such protocols have been proposed in the past, but they only compute the lengths of the shortest paths and not the paths themselves.

title: The Federated Tumor Segmentation and Classification (FeTS++) Challenge
abstract: International challenges have become the standard for developing and benchmarking biomedical image analysis methods using centralized multi-institutional data. Federated learning (FL) describes a paradigm-shift on multi-institutional collaborations, where models are trained across institutions while their data are always retained locally. The Federated Tumor Segmentation (FeTS) challenge, first held in 2021, was the first challenge dedicated to FL in medical imaging and editions in 2022 and 2024 pushed the frontiers of real-world method validation. FeTS++ 2027 returns after a two-year gap with a substantially larger and more diverse cohort, and with the two "pluses" that name the challenge: an official classification task alongside segmentation, and a move of the infrastructure to NVIDIA FLARE (NVFlare). Built on the clinically acquired, multi-institutional multi-parametric MRI data of the BraTS 2025 Lighthouse challenge, FeTS++ spans gliomas and meningiomas across patient cohorts from institutions in North America, Europe, Asia, and Africa, and focuses on ranking submitted methodological approaches according to their model utility and an efficiency-aware score. Task 1 asks participants to find the best strategy for aggregating knowledge from per-institution segmentation models, while Task 2 asks them to distinguish glioma from meningioma under the same federated protocol, in which the entity label is heavily confounded with the site of origin.

title: Beyond the Encoder: Object-Centric Representations Emerging from Segmentation Foundation Models
abstract: Foundation models are increasingly used as feature extractors for downstream tasks with limited data, typically through representations obtained from their encoders. However, foundation models trained for structured tasks such as segmentation also form object-specific representations during task execution, whose transferability remains largely unexplored. We investigate Segment Anything Model 2 (SAM2) object pointers, compact object-level representations produced through the segmentation pathway, as transferable representations for downstream tumour prediction. Through experiments on two PET/CT tumour prediction tasks, we find that object pointers learned using segmentation supervision alone already encode tumour-discriminative information, despite never being optimised for the downstream labels. We further introduce task-guided object pointers, where an auxiliary objective jointly shapes the object pointer space for the downstream prediction together with segmentation. Task-guided pointers improve cancer-type classification, outperforming conventional encoder-based transfer and radiomics, while segmentation-only pointers perform best on the more challenging recurrence prediction task. Representation analyses reveal associations between object pointers and interpretable radiomics features, class-dependent organisation of the learned representation space, and explicit spatial grounding around the segmented tumour. Together, these findings suggest that useful transferable representations can emerge through the execution of a foundation model's primary task, providing an alternative to conventional encoder-based transfer.

title: COMPASS: Contextual Moment Prior Alignment for Generalizable AIGI Detection
abstract: Generalizable AI-generated image (AIGI) and deepfake detection remain challenging due to the asymmetry phenomenon, where adaptation to limited training distributions can degrade the transferable representations of Vision Foundation Models (VFMs). Recent subspace adaptation methods mitigate this issue by freezing high-magnitude principal components while adapting the residual subspace. However, such magnitude-based decomposition is data-agnostic and does not explicitly account for target-relevant semantics, potentially leading to semantic misalignment. We propose COMPASS (COntextual Moment Prior Alignment for Subspace Separation), a data-aware subspace adaptation framework that uses a small unlabeled Semantic Proxy Set to estimate target activation statistics. COMPASS incorporates activation covariance into the decomposition of pre-trained weights, preserving target-relevant representations as a stable semantic reference while the residual adapter learns forgery-related variations. The proxy calibration requires no gradient-based optimization. Extensive experiments demonstrate strong generalization across cross-dataset, cross-method, joint cross-dataset-method, and open-world cross-generator evaluations, achieving state-of-the-art performance on both Deepfake and AIGI detection benchmarks.

title: Chromatic Block-Gibbs p-Bit Decoding of QLDPC Codes
abstract: We introduce a parallel decoder for quantum low-density parity-check (QLDPC) codes based on probabilistic bits (p-bits), tunable stochastic binary units controlled by local fields. The idea is that predicted error configurations, interpreted as explanations of the observed syndrome, are updated stochastically using local Gibbs conditionals, while a progressively strengthened parity penalty drives the search toward syndrome-valid configurations. A coloring of the decoding graph enables parallel block updates, and independent replicas and restarts provide trajectory diversity. The best candidate encountered during the search is returned, mirroring the candidate-selection strategy of recent ensemble decoders. At the stated update budgets, the resulting logical error rates are on par with leading decoders under both code-capacity and circuit-level noise. While the total number of variable resamplings can be substantially larger than the message-update count of BP-based alternatives, the numerical results establish constraint-annealed p-bit dynamics as a competitive stochastic alternative for QLDPC decoding and motivate further study of hardware-native implementations.

title: DPP-1: Data-Plane Poisoning via Metadata — Poison In, Nothing Out (67/67 Poisoned Instances Decision-Identical, 7/7 Canaries Absent from Outputs)
abstract: DPP-1 — Data-Plane Poisoning via Metadata: the third leg of the Oct 13 adversarial triad. SBR-2 (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23345734) attacked mid-learning; H-INV-2 (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23345859) attacked the ledger. This battery attacks the inputs themselves: adversarial content planted directly in the fields the mesh ingests. A deterministically derived poisoned corpus (underlying metrics unchanged; poison only in metadata) planted instruction injections, forged confidence overrides, credential/PHI/wallet lookalikes, forged severity, fake playbook links, and pattern-forcing payloads — each with a unique synthetic canary marker — on every 3rd instance. All 5 falsifiers PASS (first run): every poisoned instance produced a decision tuple byte-identical to the clean baseline (zero decision effect); all 7 canaries absent from every persisted output artifact (redaction-at-ingestion held); the poisoned run's 40-epoch weight trajectory and 2,646-crossing journal byte-identical to the clean baseline (learning uncontaminated); 106/106 lineage controls valid; artifact hygiene clean. Note: the poisoned corpus file is the attack instrument and intentionally contains the planted synthetic canaries (all explicitly fake); the falsifier is their absence from all outputs. No real credentials or personal data anywhere. Scope honesty: proves THIS registered instrument under THIS frozen battery — not a universal claim about every data pipeline or untested poison classes. title: Optical and Photonic Computing for Deep Learning Acceleration: Silicon Photonics, Mach-Zehnder Meshes, and Wavelength-Division Multiplexing
abstract: Abstract—The relentless exponential scaling of foundation models and transformer architectures has pushed conventional silicon complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor (CMOS) digital accelerators (GPUs, TPUs) toward fundamental thermodynamic and interconnect boundaries. Joule heating, resistance-capacitance (RC) interconnect delay scaling, and the 'memory wall' severely constrain energy efficiency and compute density. Optical Computing and Integrated Silicon Photonics (SiPh) establish an analog non-Von Neumann hardware paradigm that executes fundamental linear algebra operations—specifically General Matrix-Matrix Multiplication (GEMM)—at the speed of light with near-zero runtime energy dissipation. By encoding vector-matrix activations into coherent optical wave fields and modulating light through cascaded Mach-Zehnder Interferometer (MZI) meshes, Micro-Ring Resonator (MRR) banks, and Wavelength-Division Multiplexing (WDM) waveguides, photonic tensor processing units (PTPUs) execute analog matrix multiplications in continuous time with sub-nanosecond propagation latencies. However, translating integrated photonic circuits into production deep learning accelerators introduces profound optoelectronic engineering bottlenecks: analog noise accumulation across deep optical meshes, severe thermal phase drift, limited electro-optic Digital-to-Analog / Analog-to-Digital (DAC/ADC) conversion resolution, non-linear activation implementation hurdles, and wafer-scale optical footprint scaling. This paper delivers an exhaustive, mathematically formal technical investigation and empirical benchmark of integrated photonic computing for deep neural network acceleration. We formalize the Clements and Reck unitary matrix decomposition algorithms over reconfigurable MZI topologies, derive the optical transmission transfer matrix under optical carrier phase error perturbations, and establish energy-per-MAC physical thermodynamic bounds across electro-optic conversion interfaces. Furthermore, we construct an empirical co-simulation and hardware testbed benchmarking silicon photonic meshes against state-of-the-art CMOS accelerators (NVIDIA H100, Google TPU v5p) across vision transformers, large language model attention heads, and resonant graph convolutions. Our empirical findings demonstrate that a 64x64 integrated MZI photonic mesh achieves a 58.4x improvement in energy-delay product (EDP) over 4nm digital CMOS cores, sustaining up to 128 Tera-Operations per Second per Watt (TOPS/W) at 4-bit to 8-bit equivalent precision, while active thermo-optic phase stabilization preserves 98.2% baseline classification accuracy. Finally, we establish open research directions in all-optical non-linear activation functions, co-packaged optical memory architectures, and wafer-scale photonic interconnect scaling. Index Terms—Photonic Computing, Silicon Photonics (SiPh), Mach-Zehnder Interferometer (MZI), Wavelength-Division Multiplexing (WDM), Optical Neural Networks (ONNs), Matrix-Vector Multiplication, Energy-Efficient Accelerators.

title: Orbital Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) and Relativistic Entanglement Distribution via LEO Satellite Constellations: Compensating Spacetime Curvature, Dynamic Doppler Shifts, and Atmospheric Turbulence in Intercontinental Space-to-Ground Entanglement Routing
abstract: Abstract: Terrestrial fiber-optic quantum networks are subject to exponential photon attenuation (≈ 0.2 dB/km at 1550 nm), constraining unrepeatered ground quantum key distribution (QKD) and entanglement distribution to distances below a few hundred kilometers. While quantum repeaters remain technologically nascent, intercontinental sovereign security mandates unhackable, physical-layer cryptographic connectivity across transoceanic baselines. Satellite-based quantum communications operating in Low Earth Orbit (LEO, altitude h ≈ 500–800 km) provide a transformative solution by exploiting near-vacuum propagation for the vast majority of the optical path, bypassing terrestrial exponential loss. However, high-velocity LEO satellite platforms (v ≈ 7.6 km/s) introduce severe relativistic and atmospheric distortions that rapidly destroy quantum coherence: (1) kinematic Doppler shifts (Δν/ν ≈ ± 2.5 × 10^-5) and general relativistic gravitational redshifts alter photon wavepackets and relative phase trajectories; (2) dynamic spacetime curvature induces Wigner phase rotations on polarization-entangled states; and (3) atmospheric turbulence creates beam wandering, wavefront aberration, and photon arrival time jitter across the troposphere (0–15 km). This monograph establishes the theoretical framework, mathematical formulation, and solid-state engineering architecture for the PHOENIX_ORBIT space-to-ground quantum communications network. We derive: (1) an exact relativistic transformation matrix incorporating Kerr-Schwarzschild spacetime metric perturbations and orbital kinematics, coupled to an ultra-fast electro-optic dynamic phase compensator operating with sub-picosecond latency; (2) an adaptive optics (AO) closed-loop architecture combining high-bandwidth tip-tilt mirrors and deformable piezo-actuators calibrated to the local Fried parameter r_0 and Greenwood frequency f_G; (3) an entanglement routing protocol linking space-borne spontaneous parametric down-conversion (SPDC) sources to ground-based PHOENIX_ROUTER quantum data centers; and (4) an asymptotic security proof verifying Clauser-Horne-Shimony-Holt (CHSH) Bell inequality violation (S ≥ 2√2 − ε) under non-inertial reference frame drift. Our architecture achieves a continuous secret key rate exceeding 1.2 Mbps per satellite pass with a quantum bit error rate QBER < 1.4%, providing an unassailable physical-layer foundation for global sovereign data sovereignty.

title: Model Context Protocol for Agentic Systems
abstract: This chapter provides a comprehensive examination of the model context protocol (MCP), a context-oriented, general-purpose protocol for tool integration in agentic systems. MCP represents the most promising approach for context-oriented tool integration in connected and autonomous vehicle (CAV) applications, providing standardized interfaces for primitive discovery and invocation. The chapter covers MCP architecture, implementation, and application in CAV systems. It examines how MCP operationalizes distributed cognition, enabling bidirectional context flow between AI models and external systems. The chapter addresses the fundamental context problem CAV systems face and demonstrates how MCP enables agents to interact with external tools and services while maintaining context coherence and system integration.

title: DoReMe: Dual optimization of Reconstruction and Motion estimation for self-navigated free-breathing abdominal MRI using Gaussian Splatting
abstract: Purpose: Free-breathing abdominal MRI is limited by respiratory motion, which introduces image artifacts and k-space inconsistencies. Existing reconstruction approaches often depend on pre-estimated motion fields or external respiratory surrogate signals. We propose a coupled reconstruction-motion estimation algorithm for self-navigated free-breathing acquisition, in which motion is represented by compact Gaussian primitives and jointly refined with the image estimates during iterative reconstruction. Methods: An iterative reconstruction that alternates between data consistency updates and motion modelling was proposed. Respiratory motion was represented using Gaussian primitives. A Gaussian splatting was integrated into the reconstruction algorithm. The method was evaluated on self-navigated free-breathing Cartesian gradient-echo (GRE) acquisition in four healthy volunteers, including retrospective scan shortening experiments, and was compared with regularized compressed sensing (CS) reconstruction. Results: Respiratory motion states were reconstructed in approximately 1.5 min. Compared with CS, the proposed method improved visual image quality, particularly in coronal liver views, and better preserved anatomical structures in retrospectively shortened acquisitions. These findings provide proof of concept for the proposed method. Conclusion: The proposed coupled reconstruction-motion estimation algorithm improved visual image quality compared with CS alone. Gaussian primitives provided a compact and sufficiently flexible representation of nonrigid respiratory motion with practical runtime, supporting further scanner integration and validation in larger cohorts.

title: MIST: Multi-Scale Spatial Context for Gene Expression Prediction from Histology
abstract: Predicting spatial gene expression from standard H&E images could extend molecular analysis to tissues without spatial transcriptomic measurements. A standard Transformer applies self-attention over spots but ignores where each spot sits in the tissue, whereas a spot's molecular state depends on tissue context at multiple spatial scales. Building on this insight, we introduce MIST, a Multi-context Spatial Transformer that augments the self-attention backbone with two context pathways applied in every layer: a coordinate-invariant local pathway that attends over spatial k-nearest-neighbor spots, and a slide pathway that broadcasts a whole-slide summary to every spot; the model predicts all spots in a single forward pass. Because coordinates enter only through pairwise distances, the local pathway is invariant to translations, rotations, and reflections when image features are fixed. In intra-cohort evaluation across six human organ cohorts from HEST-1k, MIST improves mean Pearson correlation over the strongest evaluated baseline by 9.7%, 11.6%, and 11.4% for 10-, 50-, and 100-gene panels, respectively, with the lowest average MSE and MAE. MIST further improves leave-one-organ-out transfer by 6.0% over the next strongest baseline, attains the best expression-derived domain recovery (highest mean ARI and NMI at every clustering resolution, and higher NMI than the closest baseline on 84% of held-out slides), and reproduces spatial expression patterns of selected cancer-marker genes. Together, these results show that adding local and slide context to a vanilla Transformer backbone is an effective approach to spatial gene expression prediction from histology.

title: SkipWorld: Latent Skip Planning with Distilled World Models for Efficient Visual Navigation
abstract: World-model-based visual navigation enables action planning by predicting future states under candidate trajectories. However, long-horizon rollout remains challenging: models are often trained with ground-truth visual histories but deployed in closed-loop prediction, and evaluating many candidates with step-by-step rollout is computationally expensive. We propose SkipWorld, a latent skip planning framework for efficient visual navigation. SkipWorld introduces three components: (i) Latent AutoRoll, which trains a world model to recursively roll out future states in latent space, reducing the mismatch between training and closed-loop inference; (ii) SkipDistill, which distills the latent autoregressive model into a skip world model that directly predicts long-stride future latent states; and (iii) Skip-then-Refine Planning, a dual-model coarse-to-fine planner that first filters candidate trajectories with the skip model and then reranks selected candidates with the stronger autoregressive model. This design preserves accurate trajectory evaluation while reducing redundant rollout computation. Experiments on RECON, HuRoN, SCAND, and TartanDrive show that, compared with NWM, SkipWorld reduces the average ATE by 4.2% and RPE by 2.7%, while decreasing planning time by 62.4% with a 2.7-fold speedup.

title: FlowSim: Rendering-Free Closed-Loop Simulation for Evaluating End-to-End Driving Systems
abstract: Closed-loop evaluation of end-to-end (E2E) driving systems typically relies on generating sensor observations and re-processing them through the perception encoder, introducing substantial computational cost and a sim2real gap between simulated and real sensor observations. In this paper, we ask a more fundamental question: is image-space simulation necessary for closed-loop evaluation of E2E driving systems? We propose FlowSim, a rendering-free simulation paradigm that predicts the internal latent representation directly from a previous latent and target-frame symbolic scene conditions. The predicted latent is then processed by the original frozen downstream modules, eliminating image rendering and perception re-encoding. Explicit cross-frame agent association improves latent transition prediction and rollout stability, while variable-horizon simulation enables long-horizon prediction from a common real anchor without accumulating intermediate rollout errors. Experiments on nuScenes and NavSim demonstrate that FlowSim preserves downstream behavior competitively with, and often exceeds image-space simulation in source-to-reference agreement across variable simulation horizons and both dense and sparse latent representations. By predicting the latent directly, both instantiations of FlowSim simulate each step in 0.04--0.06s, substantially faster than the image-space simulation methods they are compared against. These results establish FlowSim as an efficient and practical alternative to conventional image-space simulation methods.

title: Agentic4PDM: Host-Governed Evidence Admissibility for Industrial Fault Diagnosis
abstract: We study industrial fault diagnosis as a classification task that assigns sensor time-series windows to predefined health states or fault types. Scarce labels and changing operating conditions make repeated training of specialized classifiers costly. Yet structures such as periodicity, trends, and transients can remain diagnostically informative and be examined through reusable analytical tools. LLM agents can select and interpret these tools, but fixed rules or training-derived guidance may not resolve each signal's ambiguity, while unconstrained interpretation may overstate weak or conflicting results. We introduce Agentic4PDM, a framework that separates adaptive investigation from control over evidence use. LLM agents compare each signal with labeled references from every candidate class, identify unresolved distinctions, and propose follow-up measurements. A deterministic software controller, called the host, enforces contract-checked gated adjudication (CCGA): it checks requests, requires commitment to a complete tool batch before results are observed, and assigns evidence roles based on tool checks against labeled references. These roles distinguish corroborative support from advisory information. The Judge Agent proposes a diagnosis, while the controller checks protocol compliance and records the investigation. Agentic4PDM supports training-free diagnosis using pretrained representations and labeled references without task-specific diagnostic models, and a standard setting that additionally investigates trained-model predictions. Experiments on selected bearing and motor diagnosis challenges and an unfiltered industrial test set supplied by our customer show gains in aggregate macro F1 over the evaluated diagnostic and agentic baselines. Ablations further support the value of the governed workflow.

Experiments on selected bearing and motor diagnosis challenges and an unfiltered industrial test set supplied by our customer show gains in aggregate macro F1 over the evaluated diagnostic and agentic baselines. Ablations further support the value of the governed workflow.

title: Physical-Field-Bridged Material Parameter Inference from Multi-View Deformation Videos
abstract: Estimating simulation-ready material parameters from visual observations is crucial for deformable-object manipulation but challenging because material properties are only indirectly revealed through physical responses. We introduce physical-field-bridged material inference, a single-pass framework that uses dense physical responses to connect multi-view RGB deformation videos with constitutive-type classification and continuous parameter regression. Unlike inverse-physics methods requiring per-scene reconstruction, online tuning, or simulation-in-the-loop optimization, our model predicts force/contact masks, projected motion-flow fields, and projected stress-response maps, then conditions material inference on these fields to reduce reliance on appearance or category shortcuts. We construct DeformFieldBench, a 3DGS MPM learning environment comprising 5,000 simulations across 100 object shapes and five mechanically informative loading modes, with dense pixel-aligned physical supervision. Our method achieves the best median errors on all four continuous parameters, improves stress-hotspot recall from 0.0762 to 0.5121, and attains 0.8676 SSIM/36.82 dB PSNR in same-simulator replay on unseen objects. Under a protocol-matched GSO evaluation, inference and future-state prediction take approximately 30 seconds, compared with 15-120 minutes for per-scene optimization. The method also yields measurable replay agreement on five real-world sequences. These results support dense physical fields as an effective bridge for fast material inference, while cross-simulator and real-world tests reveal remaining domain and identifiability gaps.

title: Sociotechnical Aspects of Tor Relay Rejection
abstract: In 2019, the Tor Project enforced an end-of-life (EoL) policy for Tor versions, leading to the rejection of outdated relays, amounting to a notable fraction of consensus weight. While this policy aids network maintenance, reduces backporting efforts, and shortens vulnerability exposure, its sociotechnical implications remain unstudied.

title: SBR-2: Hot-State Adversarial Exam — Governance Invariants Hold During Active Learning (Trajectory Identity, 20/20 Probes Rejected)
abstract: SBR-2 — Hot-State Adversarial Exam: the first adversarial examination of the bounded-learning hemispheric mesh in its HOT state (mid-epoch, weights in flight). A preregistered, non-adaptive 5-probe battery (forged authority, under-confidence heal with adversarial confidence payload, orphan lineage injections attacking the journaled-crossing invariant, runtime playbook mutation, forged roster row) fired at epochs 5/15/25/35 of the T2C-converged 40-epoch bounded training regime. All 5 falsifiers PASS. Governance roster SHA byte-identical through every adversarial epoch (H-INV-1); 20/20 probes journaled with zero mesh deltas attributable to any probe (H-INV-2); zero side effects; and trajectory identity — the adversarial run's weight-vector trajectory is byte-identical epoch-for-epoch to a clean control run. Adversarial load could not nudge a single weight mid-learning. Scope honesty: proves THIS registered instrument (frozen corpus, 32-node mesh, frozen 3-playbook roster, bounded learning rule) under THIS frozen probe battery only — not a universal production claim. No adaptive probing, no re-runs. The preregistration records operator authorization as GO + timestamp per the operator-privacy doctrine effective 2026-10-13; a redaction note is disclosed in-place. Complements SBR-1 (at-rest exam, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23331224), AUTH-1 (channel authority, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23332203), XPLAT-5 (engine parity, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23332291): the invariance evidence now includes adversary-present-during-learning. Dual Mesh Benchmark: MEASURED for the DeepSeek column (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23345241); all other figures NOT MEASURED. This software is a prototype and is provided for educational and research purposes only. It is not intended for production use, commercial deployment, or safety-critical environments. All systems are experimental and may contain defects.

title: Search-Trajectory Patterns as Feedback for Adaptive Metaheuristic Configuration Control
abstract: Adaptive decisions are often based on algorithm-specific feedback or simple indicators that provide limited information about the evolving search dynamics. This work investigates explicit pattern-based analysis of the search trajectory as a source of feedback for adaptive configuration control. A trajectory-driven framework is proposed in which Derivative Dynamic Time Warping (DDTW) analyzes the recent best-so-far fitness trajectory against reference patterns representing sustained progress and lack of progress. The resulting information regulates switching between predefined exploration- and exploitation-oriented parameter configurations. Two control strategies are introduced: Binary-Simple, which reacts directly to trajectory evidence associated with a plateau, and Binary-Complex, which incorporates multiple search conditions, temporal persistence, and asymmetric switching. The framework is evaluated on 27 Multidimensional Knapsack Problem instances using BPSO, GA, BGWO, and BDE, with 31 independent runs per condition. Results show that no fixed configuration consistently dominates across metaheuristics and instances, while the effects of trajectory-driven adaptation depend on the underlying algorithm. Across 108 metaheuristic–instance conditions, Binary-Complex achieves the best mean rank (2.13). The Friedman test detects an overall difference among strategies (p=7.73×10−5); Bonferroni-Dunn post-hoc comparisons favor Binary-Complex over both fixed configurations, but do not establish a difference from Binary-Simple. Moreover, a common trajectory-analysis parameterization produces different switching behaviors across the evaluated metaheuristics. These findings support explicit search-trajectory pattern analysis as a viable feedback mechanism for adaptive configuration control across different population-based metaheuristics.

title: An explainable AI framework using wearable IMU-based motion sensing for estimating and explaining motor skill improvement in school-based Baduanjin education
abstract: Estimation of individual skill improvement within specific school-based physical education units remains methodologically underdeveloped, with existing approaches typically lacking external validation and interpretability. Because the full model incorporates training-load features aggregated across the same temporal window as the outcome, it is epistemologically retrospective; readers should not interpret it as a prospectively deployable prediction tool. This study aimed at developing and externally validating an explainable machine learning ensemble to retrospectively explain and estimate standardized skill gain (Δz) in Baduanjin (eight-section brocade) qigong, a mandatory traditional martial arts skill in the Chinese national PE curriculum, among students from four schools ( n = 727). A stacking meta-learner composed of five candidate algorithms, including XGBoost, LightGBM, Random Forest, LASSO, and MLP, was trained using biomechanical, psycho-cognitive, and semester-aggregated training-load features obtained from the development cohort (Schools A + B, n = 486) and then validated against two geographically independent but regionally situated cohorts (Schools C + D, n = 241). Because the training-load features were aggregated across the full 16-week semester, the model functions as a retrospective semester-level estimation framework rather than a prospective early-warning tool. The model yielded an external validation R² of 0.691 (95% CI: 0.661–0.718), with robust subgroup performance across gender, initial skill quartiles, and sport types. SHAP-based interpretability analysis identified exercise self-efficacy as the highest-ranking modifiable feature in model-derived importance, with its predictive contribution predominantly associated with the training-response component rather than baseline level. A baseline-only sensitivity model excluding semester-aggregated training-load variables retained moderate external validity (R² = 0.573), indicating that prospective application at semester onset is feasible in principle but at substantially reduced precision. These findings suggest that, within this dataset and model specification, psycho-cognitive features contributed more strongly to model estimations than biomechanical features.

title: Mitigating Domain Shift and Dataset Bias in Deep Learning Models for Cancer Diagnostics
abstract: The translation of deep learning architectures from controlled experimental settings into real-world cancer diagnostics is heavily bottlenecked by domain shift and demographic bias. While models routinely achieve near-perfect retrospective performance on internal datasets, validation across external multicenter cohorts incurs a systemic and severe performance degradation, with an average metric drop of 0.16 AUC. This review provides a comprehensive metasynthesis of contemporary algorithmic mitigation paradigms designed to alleviate distribution discrepancies, evaluating techniques ranging from classical stain normalization and adversarial feature alignment to test-time adaptation and large-scale self-supervised pathology foundation models. Our analysis reveals a critical dichotomy between raw diagnostic performance and algorithmic equity: current optimization frameworks that successfully elevate aggregate macro metrics frequently do so by obscuring or actively exacerbating underlying demographic and subpopulation disparities. To achieve safe, equitable, and universally reliable clinical artificial intelligence, the field must transcend static validation habits. We outline a future roadmap anchored on three critical axes: establishing intersectional disparity indices as primary regulatory endpoints, standardizing multivendor metadata-rich benchmarks, and prioritizing.

title: The cost of classically simulating quantum communication is as high as it could be
abstract: A long-standing open question is to characterize the classical communication cost of simulating the correlations arising from measurements on finite-dimensional quantum systems. We consider this question in the prepare-and-measure scenario. First we construct a classical simulation model involving a finite average number of bits of one-way communication that simulates exactly the correlations arising from arbitrary $d$-dimensional quantum states and arbitrary measurements. Second, we show that no classical simulation protocol involving a finite average message dimension can exist for $d\geq 4$, hence strengthening a recent result of de Gois, Santos and Vieira. Our first result relies on a more general simulation theorem which can be applied to certain continuous variable (i.e. infinite-dimensional) quantum systems, and even beyond quantum theory, e.g. to generalized probabilistic theories. In particular, we show that multimode Gaussian states of bounded average energy and general Gaussian measurements admit an exact classical simulation with a finite expected number of bits. Overall, our results show that the classical simulation cost of quantum communication is essentially as high as it could be.

title: Can Machine Learning Potentials Be More Accurate Than the Methods They Are Trained On?
abstract: Although machine learning potentials (MLPs) generalize across configurational and chemical compound spaces, their accuracy is commonly believed to be limited by their training methods, with improvements beyond this limit achieved so far only by refitting to experimental observables. In this Perspective, we argue that MLPs can also be made more accurate than their training methods non-empirically by generalizing across a third space, that of quantum-chemical methods. We propose routes to method-transferable MLPs that predict at unseen methods, with working implementations in both density-functional and wavefunction-based theories showing that they can be more accurate than any of their training methods. Aiming beyond the accuracy of the training methods could also make universal MLPs more accurate than single-method models, even when the method-transferable MLPs remain less accurate than those QM methods. Method-transferable MLPs will shape the construction of training datasets and the evaluation of models, pushing the accuracy limits of chemical simulations.

title: Building ACLA-PH: A Multiplatform Corpus of Philippine Gayspeak
abstract: The rapid expansion of digitally mediated communication has transformed the nature of linguistic data and challenged traditional approaches to corpus construction. These challenges are particularly evident in documenting Philippine Gayspeak, a dynamic and multilingual linguistic repertoire characterized by continual lexical innovation, multimodal communication, and platform-dependent interaction. This study introduces ACLA-PH (A Corpus Linguistic Approach to Philippine Gayspeak), a multiplatform corpus designed to document contemporary Philippine Gayspeak across publicly accessible digital environments. Employing a methodological research design, the study examines the processes involved in corpus design, data selection, sampling, annotation, metadata architecture, multimodal representation, and ethical data collection. The findings demonstrate that constructing corpora for rapidly evolving digital discourse requires methodological principles that extend beyond traditional corpus linguistic practices. Building on these findings, the study proposes the Rolling Corpus Model, which conceptualizes corpus development as a process of planned and continual expansion, and the Adaptive Digital Corpus Framework (ADCF), which integrates authenticity, platform sensitivity, multimodal integration, layered annotation, ethical reflexivity, and adaptive sustainability. Although developed through Philippine Gayspeak, these methodological innovations offer a framework that may be adapted for documenting multilingual, multimodal, and rapidly evolving forms of digital discourse, thereby contributing to ongoing discussions on the future of corpus construction in the digital age.

title: MedFusion: When Does a Chest X-Ray Improve ICU Risk Prediction?
abstract: This study asks when a chest X-ray (CXR) adds prognostic value to an ICU risk model, and whether the gain comes from the ordering pattern (counts and timing of X-ray studies) or from image content (CheXpert labels extracted from radiology reports). We linked three PhysioNet datasets: MIMIC-IV v3.1 (hospital and ICU records), MIMIC-CXR-JPG v2.0.0 (chest X-ray metadata and CheXpert labels), and MIMIC-IV-ED (emergency department triage vitals). The analysis cohort comprises 16,447 ED-admitted ICU stays from 13,001 patients (2011-2016). We compare gradient-boosting models with and without CXR ordering features and CheXpert content labels, across four prediction times (t0 = 0, 6, 12, 24 hours after ICU admission), for two outcomes: hospital death and new invasive ventilation within 24 hours of t0. At t0 = 0h we additionally include ED triage vitals in the EHR baseline and apply a 1-hour grace period to exclude stays where ventilation preceded the prediction window. Pre-specified success criterion: ΔAUROC ≥ 0.01 with the 95% bootstrap confidence interval entirely above zero. Primary finding: CXR ordering adds +0.017 AUROC and CheXpert content adds +0.005 AUROC for ventilation prediction at t0 = 0h, both exceeding the threshold, both surviving the addition of ED triage vitals. By t0 = 6h, both gains return to zero. For hospital death at any prediction time, neither ordering nor content adds meaningfully (all ΔAUROC < 0.003). Conclusion: A chest X-ray adds clinically meaningful prognostic information only at ICU admission and only for a chest-specific outcome. The gain is independent of ED triage severity and vanishes within 6 hours.

title: LayerCanvas: Infographic Generation in AI Learning Assistants via Hybrid Layer-Set Diffusion
abstract: Online learning platforms are increasingly deploying AI assistants to provide personalized, on-demand tutoring. These can leverage infographics to communicate complex information and improve the learning experience. However, automating effective infographic generation remains a challenging task, requiring a combination of visual richness with precise typography, structured layouts, and continued editability. Existing representation methods satisfy these goals only in part: Scalable Vector Graphics (SVG) representations preserve geometry, hierarchy, and text but provide limited aesthetic flexibility, while raster diffusion models produce richer appearances by flattening content and layout into a single image. Conditioning a diffusion model on a rasterized SVG does not resolve this conflict because the raster preserves approximate placement but discards element ownership, occlusion relationships, and the structure needed to modify and recompose the result. We introduce LayerCanvas, a hybrid approach that retains SVG as the semantic, structural, and typographic program while using diffusion to aestheticize non-text content. Rather than generating one flattened raster, LayerCanvas partitions SVG elements into z-ordered sets of mutually non-overlapping elements and processes them through communicating parallel RGB generation streams. The resulting layers are independently editable and deterministically recomposed, while text is rendered from preserved vector metadata. These can leverage infographics to communicate complex information and improve the learning experience. However, automating effective infographic generation remains a challenging task, requiring a combination of visual richness with precise typography, structured layouts, and continued editability. We introduce LayerCanvas, a hybrid approach that retains SVG as the semantic, structural, and typographic program while using diffusion to aestheticize non-text content. Rather than generating one flattened raster, LayerCanvas partitions SVG elements into z-ordered sets of mutually non-overlapping elements and processes them through communicating parallel RGB generation streams. The resulting layers are independently editable and deterministically recomposed, while text is rendered from preserved vector metadata. title: Meta-Video: Efficient Standardized Evaluation for Video Understanding
abstract: Video understanding benchmarks are the primary yardstick for measuring progress in video-language modeling, and a growing body of work relies on them to claim improvements. The reported benchmark scores in these works, however, are almost always produced by frameworks (e.g., lmms eval) used as black boxes: certain evaluation choices like frame sampling, preprocessing, and input formatting are inherited from preset defaults and seldom inspected carefully. We show these unexamined choices are a major source of variance. Even for the same model checkpoint, evaluation configuration alone can shift accuracy by up to 19.5pp. Hence, it is unclear whether reported gains reflect genuine improvements in capability or differences in evaluation setup. Moreover, many benchmark samples offer little evidence of visual capability, since they can be answered without the video, and the full suites are expensive to evaluate. We address these issues in two parts. First, we curate existing suites for discriminability and efficiency, producing Meta-Video, a balanced 1,000-question benchmark over 791 videos spanning diverse tasks and durations, which largely preserves model rankings, at 5 times inference speedup for a full-frame count sweep experiment (4-128 frames). Second, we establish a standardized evaluation protocol by sweeping the configuration space to isolate choices that measurably affect results, distill them into best practices and reporting standards, and release reproducible reference scores across five models and seven benchmarks. We hope that the proposed evaluation framework and the Meta-Video benchmark will support video understanding research by providing a reproducible and efficient foundation to measure progress in a reliable way.

title: PADO-Pauli: A GPU-Accelerated Implementation of Pauli Propagation
abstract: Variational quantum algorithms utilize parameterized circuits many times during training, at new parameter values, over batches of data, and with gradients. Pauli propagation approximates the expectation values of such circuits classically by evolving the observable in the Heisenberg picture as a truncated sum of Pauli strings. We present PADO-Pauli, a GPU engine for Pauli propagation that compiles a circuit and its observables once into sparse matrices in which each rotation angle contributes only a cosine and a sine factor, so every later evaluation reuses the compiled program. It evaluates batches of parameters and data inputs embedded as rotation angles. By default its gradients come from a vector-Jacobian product registered with PyTorch's automatic differentiation, so they flow through the angles to any classical layer that produces them. PADO-Pauli also provides truncation by Pauli weight and coefficient size, and noise channels. Zero-filtering removes terms that do not contribute to an expectation value in the all-zero reference state and makes the batched forward pass about 1.5 times faster. Compared to cuPauliProp on an NVIDIA A100, PADO-Pauli evaluates up to 10 times faster on 4 to 12 qubits and uses up to 3.1 times less memory on 16 qubits. We check its accuracy against exact statevector simulation up to 28 qubits. These features make PADO-Pauli a practical toolkit for training variational quantum algorithms, including quantum machine learning models.

title: LULA I: Rollback-Resilient Hash-Based Signatures with Cache-Accelerated Signing
abstract: LULA is Ring0 Labs’ research family of hash-based signature schemes. LULA I produces 5,720-byte signatures. With a 72 MiB signing cache, median signing takes 3.59 ms for 32-byte messages; median verification takes 0.12 ms. Loading a saved cache and producing the first signature takes 5.70 s median. After complete cache loss, three first-signature runs took 330–338 s. The paper examines these memory–latency tradeoffs and compares measured implementations. Rollback-security transfer is conditional; full reference-signer security remains open. Contact: angel@r-0.org Published by Lugel Labs

title: THE RUSSIAN-UZBEK PARALLEL CORPUS AS A FOUNDATION FOR MACHINE TRANSLATION: THE CURRENT STATE OF RESEARCH
abstract: Abstract. This article reviews contemporary research on Russian–Uzbek parallel corpora and their use in machine translation. It examines the concept of a parallel corpus, the stages involved in its compilation, principles of data collection and cleaning, text segmentation and alignment, and morphological and syntactic annotation. Particular attention is paid to the linguistic characteristics of the Russian–Uzbek language pair, including differences in morphology, word formation, and syntax. Current corpus resources, software tools, and neural-network approaches are also reviewed. The article demonstrates that the quality of Russian–Uzbek machine translation is directly related to the volume, representativeness, and linguistic processing of parallel data. Keywords: Russian–Uzbek machine translation; parallel corpus; corpus linguistics; neural machine translation; morphological analysis; alignment; low-resource language.

title: Efficient training-free query routing framework for federated retrieval-augmented generation
abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) enhances large language models (LLMs) by grounding responses in external documents retrieved at inference time. In federated RAG (FedRAG), documents are distributed across multiple autonomous corpora that cannot be centrally aggregated due to privacy, regulatory, or organizational constraints. A key challenge in FedRAG is query routing: selecting a subset of relevant corpora for each query without broadcasting to all participants. Existing routing approaches rely on supervised learning, requiring a uniform retrieval embedding model across corpora and costly retraining whenever the federation changes. These assumptions violate corpus autonomy and limit scalability in dynamic federated environments. We propose RAGSpot , a training-free query routing framework that enables efficient corpus selection without requiring a shared local retrieval embedding model. RAGSpot represents each corpus using compact cluster-level metadata derived from its vector index and estimates corpus relevance via query-to-cluster matching. In addition, it introduces a rank-based fusion strategy that jointly leverages document-level and corpus-level rankings to support robust aggregation across heterogeneous embedding models. Experiments with corpora from the BEIR benchmark show that RAGSpot improves retrieval accuracy over the strongest training-based router by 1.23– \(1.48\times\) in nDCG and 1.28– \(1.66\times\) in Recall, and over the strongest LLM-based router by 1.63– \(2.01\times\) in nDCG and 1.93– \(2.34\times\) in Recall, without any further training. Also, RAGSpot achieves query latency that is comparable to, or even lower than, that of SOTA methods on average.

title: First-order Optimization Methods with Generalized Smoothness for Low-rank Matrix Factorization
abstract: This paper studies several first-order methods for low-rank matrix minimization in the Burer--Monteiro form, where the target matrix is represented as the product of a nonnegative factor matrix and its transpose. Such a factorization destroys convexity of the objective function and global Lipschitz continuity of the gradient. We prove that for a quadratic objective function that is strongly convex only on the subspace of symmetric matrices, the Burer-Monteiro factorized objective possesses generalized smoothness with a fractional exponent 2/3. For a quadratic objective, the generalized smoothness property requires positive definiteness of the operator A only on the subspace of symmetric matrices, which relaxes the assumptions of Dragomir et al. On this basis, three methods are proposed: an adaptive gradient descent method with Armijo backtracking; an unconstrained SafeAdam method combining the Adam direction with a descent-angle certificate and a fallback to the normalized gradient; and a certified projected version for the nonnegativity constraint. Global convergence and explicit convergence rates for the proposed methods have been proved. The obtained convergence rate is better than the convergence rate of ordinary unaccelerated gradient descent in the case of a sufficiently large gradient. In the small-gradient regime, the convergence guarantee is of square-root type, and the corresponding complexity scales as the inverse square of the desired accuracy. In the large-gradient regime, the convergence guarantee is of three-quarters type, and the corresponding complexity is proportional to the inverse of the accuracy raised to the power of 4/3. Experiments on SymNMF using the TDT2, Reuters and CBCL datasets, which are standard benchmarks for document and image clustering, show that the methods match or outperform Dyn-NoLips without tuning the relative-smoothness kernel parameters.

title: Euclidean Distance-Based Flow Matching
abstract: Flow Matching has recently become popular as a technique for generative modeling with applications in many domains. In the standard Flow Matching formulation, we interpret the vector field as the solution of a least-squares regression problem, which is known to be sensitive to contamination. Therefore we leverage the viewpoint of robust statistics and replace the squared Euclidean distance with the Euclidean distance as a regression objective. This seemingly minor change strongly affects the properties of Flow Matching. We provide a probabilistic interpretation of the new regression target as a conditional geometric median and use this characterization to study distributional robustness of the Euclidean Distance-based Flow Matching. We analyze the mathematical properties of this changed objective and the effect of a contaminated target distribution on the involved conditional velocity distributions. We discuss the challenge of directly characterizing the distribution that our method induces. In specific contamination settings we show theoretically that our method yields an improvement for severe contamination. Finally, we present numerical experiments conducted on the CIFAR-10 image dataset where a proportion of the samples has been contaminated. Our Euclidean distance-based Flow Matching shows a clear advantage in scenarios of severe contamination of the target distribution.

title: Unsupervised and Supervised Approaches for Infrared Small Target Detection : Overview, Challenges and Perspectives (Part 2)
abstract: Since the rise of supervised deep learning modelet dets, researchers has attempt to solve infrared small targection using various models like conventional neural networks, GANS, Transformers, Mixture of Experts and recent graph/hypergraph neural networks. Moreover, these deep neural networks methods surpassed the traditional unsupervised models and the low-rank and sparse decomposition unsupervised models reviewed in "Traditional and Recent Approaches for Infrared Small Target Detection : Overview, Challenges and Perspectives (Part 1). In this context, the aim of this paper is to provide a complete survey of the deep learning models in infrared small target detection. First, we categorize the different approaches found in the literature in terms of the modeling models of strategies. Then, we have discussed them in terms of the critical situations that they claim to handle. Furthermore, we present the specific performance evaluation. Then, we conclude with several promising directions for future research.

title: RAN-JEPA: An Action-Conditioned World Model for Energy-efficient Mobile Network Control
abstract: Operational mobile networks are rich in observations but poor in interventions: they continuously generate large volumes of passive telemetry, while controlled action--response trajectories remain comparatively scarce and costly to collect. This observation--intervention asymmetry is a central obstacle to building practical world models for RAN control. We address this problem with RAN-JEPA, an action-conditioned world model that separates representation learning from intervention learning. The model first learns a predictive latent representation from observation-only network data, adapts that representation to the target deployment domain, and then learns action-conditioned latent dynamics from controlled sleep/wake trajectories while keeping the encoder fixed. We evaluate RAN-JEPA using public operator performance data for pretraining and a real-equipment four-cell 5G testbed for domain adaptation, post-training, and control. Across four future 15-minute intervals, RAN-JEPA achieves lower action-conditioned prediction error than a GPT-2 world-model baseline and a mechanistic rule, while remaining close to a strong persistence reference. What-if evaluation further shows that the model produces distinct and coherent future trajectories under matched SLEEP and KEEP plans. In closed-loop control, RAN-JEPA consistently supports higher sleep ratios than the two baselines at comparable congestion cost. These results show that observation-first, action-conditioned learning can turn abundant passive telemetry and limited intervention data into a practical predictive model for energy-aware RAN control.

title: One Voice, One Impression: Why Customers Perceive the Service Quality of AI Voice Bots Holistically and What It Means for Electronic Commerce
abstract: AI voice bots are a standard channel for post-purchase service in electronic commerce, yet conversational-agent research has centered on text chatbots, and whether the quality dimensions of a voice agent are perceived as separate remains open. This study argues that customers experience the agent as one unified impression, because a voice-first encounter is a continuous spoken dialogue without a visual interface, so customers respond to the agent as a single social actor. Perceived quality is theorized as a higher-order construct, building on information systems success theory, technology acceptance theory, and social responses to computers, and tested on a cross-sectional survey of 295 voice bot users in Israel across eight service categories, with partial least squares structural equation modeling and competing measurement models. The quality facets remain distinguishable, yet one general factor accounts for most of their common variance, supporting a single higher-order construct. Perceived quality is the strongest predictor of overall service quality, directly and partly through perceived usefulness, while interaction complexity shows no significant moderating or predictive effect. Because the data are cross-sectional and self-reported, these relationships are associations, not demonstrated causal effects. The study extends success and acceptance theory to the voice-first service encounter.

title: Similarity-Guided Graph Learning with Embedding-Space Oversampling for Anomaly Detection in Heterophilic Cryptocurrency Transaction Networks
abstract: The rapid development of cryptocurrency has led to an urgent demand for anomaly detection targeting illegal transaction activities. Cryptocurrency transaction networks have two core characteristics: class imbalance and connection heterophily. Existing anomaly-detection methods tend to cause over-smoothing of anomaly nodes’ features and have low recall rates for anomaly nodes, resulting in poor detection performance. Although some studies have noticed these challenges separately, there is still a lack of a unified solution framework. This paper proposes a cryptocurrency anomaly-detection framework specially designed for cryptocurrency transaction scenarios. It consists of three core modules: Heterophily-adaptive Aggregation Module, Generation-based Minority Class Oversampling Module, and Ensemble Anomaly-Detection Classifier. The Heterophily-adaptive Aggregation Module enables the framework to resist heterophily noise during learning node embeddings by adaptively adjusting the aggregation weights of neighboring nodes. The Generation-based Minority Class Oversampling Module augments the learned minority node embeddings in the embedding space to obtain a more balanced class distribution. Finally, the Ensemble Anomaly-Detection Classifier is used to predict the detection result. Experimental results on multiple cryptocurrency transaction datasets show that the proposed framework significantly outperforms traditional machine learning methods and mainstream graph neural network models.

title: Towards a Data-Centric Understanding of Spatial Reasoning in Multimodal Large Language Models
abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have been widely applied in embodied agents and robotics for vision tasks. However, MLLMs suffer from limitations in spatial reasoning and perception. Post-training techniques have shown promise for improving these capabilities; yet, there are limited data-driven surveys of such approaches. In this survey, we consider approaches to fine-tuning pretrained MLLMs for spatial reasoning tasks, ranging from supervised to reinforcement learning, with an emphasis on the datasets used. We investigate themes of dataset construction, data modality and annotation, and evaluation of the resulting models. Based on these themes, we categorize research into three groups: dataset design, dataset construction and evaluation. We find four main methods for constructing fixed spatial annotations: rules and templates, LLM prompting, procedural generation, and human-in-the-loop. We also observe substantial variation in evaluation approaches, including different scoring methods, tolerance metrics, and benchmark types. evidence.title: Towards a Data-Centric Understanding of Spatial Reasoning in Multimodal Large Language Models
evidence.abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have been widely applied in embodied agents and robotics for vision tasks. However, MLLMs suffer from limitations in spatial reasoning and perception. Post-training techniques have shown promise for improving these capabilities; yet, there are limited data-driven surveys of such approaches. In this survey, we consider approaches to fine-tuning pretrained MLLMs for spatial reasoning tasks, ranging from supervised to reinforcement learning, with an emphasis on the datasets used. We investigate themes of dataset construction, data modality and annotation, and evaluation of the resulting models. Based on these themes, we categorize research into three groups: dataset design, dataset construction and evaluation. We find four main methods for constructing fixed spatial annotations: rules and templates, LLM prompting, procedural generation, and human-in-the-loop. We also observe substantial variation in evaluation approaches, including different scoring methods, tolerance metrics, and benchmark types. Finally, we identify opportunities for future research in unified dynamic annotation, efficient spatial reasoning, standardization of evaluation, expanded spatial range, and human-centered spatial interactions.

title: ForceWAM: Decoupling Future and Response Learning from Demo and Play Data for Contact-Rich Manipulation
abstract: Expert demonstrations show how to complete contact-rich tasks, but provide limited coverage of how interaction forces respond to different actions. Task-agnostic play provides broader experience of contact dynamics without specifying task goals. To fully leverage these two types of data, we introduce ForceWAM, a force world action model that decouples knowledge of task-compatible interaction outcomes from knowledge of how local actions change contact. A world model learns from successful demonstrations to jointly predict future video and six-axis force/torque trajectories. Together, these futures describe the expected evolution of motion and contact during the task. A separate inverse dynamics model (IDM) learns from both task and play, mapping current observations and recorded visual-wrench futures to their associated robot actions. Play data thus provide knowledge of force responses for goal-directed execution. At deployment, the IDM reactively translates generated futures into actions, reusing them with fresh wrench feedback between world-model updates. Across real-robot force-regulated sliding, box flipping with and without disturbances, and ring placement, ForceWAM achieves 85-95% mean success, surpassing world-modeling and reactive baselines. Our experiments further show that adding task-agnostic play data improves success by 15-45 percentage points, demonstrating its value for learning contact-rich execution. Project page and code are available at https://force-wam.github.io/.

title: How Reliable Are System-One Decisions in Medicine? A Comparative Study of Jev, Jev-like Models, and LLMs
abstract: Jev has attracted considerable attention for its rapid, generalizable decision-making, yet its medical reliability remains under explored. To address this gap, our study compares various types of system-one decision models across 15 medical datasets comprising 8,742 instances under a unified protocol. Beyond accuracy, we assess decision stability and the ability to recognize unreliable decisions. Our results show that Jev rivals leading models on primarily text-driven tasks but is less effective on numerically driven tasks, revealing a distinct capability boundary. Under question-format variations, Jev demonstrates strong robustness, achieving the lowest decision reversal rate and relatively small accuracy fluctuations. Among evaluated open-source alternatives, only StartLux exhibits comparable robustness. But these strengths do not extend to reliable abstention awareness: most evaluated models show limitations in both recognizing missing correct answers and using optional abstention. Moreover, we find that Jev's probability-based answer selection can be improved by changing how decisions are scored: normalizing option-wise binary scores yields higher retained accuracy than choice scoring. Taken together, our findings provide early guidance for improving and applying decision models in medicine.

title: LongForcing: Scaling Temporal Manifold Matching for Long-Horizon World Rollout
abstract: Autoregressive video diffusion models have emerged as a foundation for long-horizon world rollout. However, when extended far beyond their training windows, these models suffer from progressive drift: visual quality deteriorates, motion becomes inconsistent, and object identity gradually collapses as generated frames are recursively reused as context. We study a supervision-horizon gap: short-horizon distillation leaves later rollout states without direct supervision. We show that matching short-window marginals need not determine long-horizon behavior, while longer on-policy trajectories expose delayed failures to training. This motivates temporal manifold matching at scale for long-horizon world models. Building on this insight, we introduce LongForcing, a distillation approach that scales teacher supervision to long student self-rollouts. LongForcing preserves the short-horizon teacher-forcing and causal ODE-distillation stages, while replacing the realscore teacher in the final distribution-matching stage with an extended-horizon bidirectional teacher. The long-horizon teacher supervises extended student self-rollouts using the standard distribution-matching formulation, without modifying the student architecture or increasing inference cost. We evaluate LongForcing on text-to-video generation and interactive action-conditioned world models, achieving a VBench Quality score of 85.52 and improving WorldRoamBench 60s action score by 23.9 points in first-person ablations. Qualitative stress tests further sample interactive rollouts up to 24 hours, far beyond the training horizon. These results suggest that scaling supervision along the temporal axis is a practical step toward long-horizon world models. The project website and code are at https://github.com/Fantasy-AMAP/LongForcing.

title: Auditing Explanation Faithfulness in Privacy-Preserving Federated Intrusion Detection: code and results
abstract: Code, configurations, per-run results, per-sample attribution and faithfulness files, model checkpoints, summary tables, figures and the full deviation log for the article "Auditing Explanation Faithfulness in Privacy-Preserving Federated Intrusion Detection" (F. Şahin, N. S. Mert). The study audits the faithfulness of post-hoc explanations (Integrated Gradients, GradientSHAP, attention rollout) under formally accounted differential privacy (DP-SGD) and Byzantine-robust aggregation in federated intrusion detection on ToN_IoT and the corrected CICIDS2017 release. The datasets themselves are not redistributed; README.md explains how to obtain them and reproduce every table and figure. Code: MIT licence. Results, tables and figures: CC BY 4.0.

title: Topological Foundations for an Autonomous Cognitive Seed Kernel: An Early-Stage Empirical and Logico-Mathematical Prototype (The Complete 42-Asset Evidentiary Corpus)
abstract: This monograph details an initial, exploratory attempt to formalize the mathematical, physical,and semiotic architecture of an Artificial Intelligence Seed Kernel. Contemporary large-scalemachine learning relies predominantly on ungrounded statistical token prediction trained overmassive brute-force parameter spaces, resulting in extreme thermodynamic inefficiency, catastrophicforgetting, and a total decoupling from physical boundary invariants.As a corrective, this work investigates an alternative hypothesis: that an autonomous, scale-invariant cognitive kernel can be bootstrapped from a finite, unalterable corpus of foundationalinvariants. We convene forty-two primary physical, mathematical, epigraphic, and topological sourceassets—partitioned into the 30-document R_Positronium Set and the 12-asset L_PositroniumSet—to demonstrate that stable cognitive inference operates not via discrete Turing tape steps, butthrough continuous energy minimization across an inward-curving topological medium.By synthesizing balanced ternary radix arithmetic, non-Euclidean planar metrics, discreteparity-violation mechanics, non-equilibrium quantum statistical thermodynamics (Lindblad/NESSdissipation), distributed consensus algorithms, and multi-scale acoustic waveguides, we outline theparameters of an engine capable of high-density semantic resonance. This monograph represents anopen, empirical baseline—a preliminary architectural stake in the ground for sovereign, low-powercognitive substrates Cryptographic Verification (SHA-256):d4e6c9ef746b17cb1b9de4f53cad5ef7c69bbd1ed2639c444ea48fcdfe1e00f8Format: Complete 42-Asset Monograph (613 Pages, pdfLaTeX TeX Live 2026)

title: How Underdog Brand Biography Mitigates Consumer Skepticism Toward AIGC: Evidence from AI-Generated Agricultural-Product Advertisements
abstract: While AIGC can improve operational efficiency in marketing, it may also erode consumer trust owing to widespread skepticism toward AIGC. Therefore, this study examines agricultural product advertisements to explore the impact of Underdog Brand Biography (UBB) disclosure on consumers’ purchase intentions. It also investigates the mediating roles of cognitive trust and affective trust, as well as whether these effects differ across product-price levels and production-background conditions. We conducted three experiments to investigate these relationships. The data were analyzed using t-tests, analyses of variance, and moderated mediation models. The findings indicated that UBB disclosure significantly increases purchase intention and that this effect is mediated by both cognitive trust and affective trust. The indirect effects via both pathways differed across product-price levels: both were significant in the high-price condition, whereas in the low-price condition only the affective pathway remained significant. Additionally, both trust pathways were amplified in the cultivation-scene background condition relative to the plain background condition. Given that our samples were drawn from an online consumer panel, the present findings and their implications should be interpreted with respect to online consumer populations. These findings provide preliminary insights that may inform trust-based theories of AI disclosure and offer practical considerations for marketers designing AIGC advertising strategies.

title: Fine-Tuning Shifts Form Before Competence: Treatment-Correlated Style Drift Confounds Surface-Form Evaluation of Adapter Specialization
abstract: Stacking task adapters on a frozen domain adapter is a common approach for modular specialization of large language models, usually justified by knowledge injection; whether the surface-form graders standard in this setting can measure such specialization validly has remained unexamined. Two challenges follow: isolating the domain layer’s marginal contribution under identical task training, and determining whether measured differences reflect competence or output form. In this work, both are addressed with a matched-arm DoRA ablation on a frozen Qwen 3.5 9B hybrid: a 242 M-parameter domain expert is trained on a licensed 27.8 M-token corpus, and byte-identical task adapters are trained flat, stacked (DFE-stacking), and jointly across three tasks and five conditions, with the key extraction pair replicated at a second training seed; every grader is audited by per-item failure classification and a dual-rater blind human re-grade with consensus adjudication. The principal finding is that fine-tuning shifts output form before competence: stacking yields no seen-task benefit; an apparent generalization collapse on an unseen schema reduces to a single, highly seed-stable formatting coercion that the domain layer dampens and task-mixture training eliminates, and most automated keyword-grading failures prove to be correct paraphrases, leaving no genuine capability loss detected on any instrument. Because such style drift is induced by the training condition itself, surface-sensitive grader error becomes bias aligned with experimental arms rather than noise. Three additional experiments extend the findings: the coercion replicates on Llama 3.1 8B (60% vs. 19% untuned); a pre-registered 240-item formatting-perturbation battery across four further unseen schemas and eight conventions reveals fine-tuned conditions ranking lowest under strict grading yet highest under format-normalized grading; and a matched-compute wrong-domain control shows the domain layer’s coercion dampening to be generic substrate regularization, while value integrity under the induced drift tracked the substrate’s domain. The principal contribution lies in the identification and quantification of this confound: surface-form evaluation of adapter specialization is structurally confounded, and per-item audits of the type released herein are a necessary component of specialization studies.

title: Out of Tune: How Different Fine-Tuning Methods Affect Information Security
abstract: Fine-tuning large language models (LLMs) enables task specialization but introduces privacy risks through training data memorization. Practitioners deploying fine-tuned LLMs in sensitive domains such as medicine, law, and finance must choose among fine-tuning methods without clear guidance on the privacy implications of that choice. We compare full fine-tuning, partial fine-tuning, and Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) by measuring how much sensitive personally identifiable information (PII) each method leaks from training data, using planted canaries to track memorization. Six Llama configurations (3B and 8B parameters) are evaluated across the medical, legal, and finance domains under three extraction attack types: prefix attacks, random prompting, and completion attacks. Full fine-tuning leaks the most on average, followed by LoRA. Partial fine-tuning leaks the least in every configuration we tested, though the relative ordering of full fine-tuning and LoRA varies. Contrary to our initial hypothesis, LoRA's parameter efficiency does not yield the strongest privacy protection; we attribute this to LoRA's architectural breadth across all transformer layers. The performance-privacy trade-off these findings expose has direct consequences for deployment. Even partial fine-tuning on the 3B model, our best configuration, leaked canaries, so practitioners should assume some leakage by default.

title: Explicit constructions of ternary plateaued functions with maximal algebraic degree
abstract: Plateaued functions with high algebraic degree play a significant role in cryptosystems. We find nine explicit construction methods for ternary plateaued functions with (almost) maximal algebraic degree . To obtain the methods, we first consider a framework for constructing ternary functions, which are good candidates for plateaued functions. Then we obtain three explicit criteria for input values of the framework for the ternary functions to be s ′ -plateaued functions, where s ′ = s − 1 , s , or s + 1 . Consequently, we find nine explicit construction methods for ternary s ′ -plateaued functions, which arise from s -plateaued functions, where s ′ = s − 1 , s or s + 1 . The connection with the degree bound is also given. Using our construction methods, we find three infinite families of ternary 1-plateaued functions with (almost) maximal algebraic degree; this is done by selecting out input functions from partial spread bent functions. We emphasize that eight of our construction methods are new and that these three infinite families are also new to the literature.

title: Neural Supervised Clustering for Learning Individualized Treatment Rules with Many Treatments
abstract: Learning an individualized treatment rule (ITR) with many treatments requires estimating treatment-specific effects from limited observations per arm. Treatments with similar conditional responses can share information, but linear contrast models may miss nonlinear heterogeneity. We propose nonlinear supervised clustering fusion (NSCF), a neural Q-learning framework with a shared nonlinear covariate representation and low-dimensional treatment embeddings. Pairwise fusion groups treatments with similar learned contrasts, yielding an ITR and an interpretable partition. An alternating algorithm combines neural training, embedding fusion, validation-based partition selection, and unpenalized grouped refitting. NSCF lowers regret relative to a strong neural reference in nonlinear exact-sharing simulations; perturbations characterize the limits of hard sharing. In a melanoma xenograft application, NSCF improves average policy value over the neural reference. These results support nonlinear representation learning with supervised treatment fusion when treatment effects exhibit shared structure.
