title: Mejoras en ocultamiento de pertenencia a comunidades mediante una arquitectura especializada de aprendizaje por refuerzo
abstract: As complex networks face increasingly advanced algorithmic analysis, the ability to conceal specific structural affiliations has emerged as a relevant graph algorithmic problem. Current online platforms rely on sophisticated techniques to characterize and cluster users in order to provide more contextualized content and services. One such approach is based on community detection algorithms applied to large underlying graphs. In this context, users are characterized by preferences or attributes, which can reveal information that may be considered sensitive. Community Membership Hiding is the problem of strategically rewiring network topology to camouflage a target node and evade detection by clustering algorithms. While recent Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) approaches have pioneered this line of work, they often face efficacy and scalability issues on large-scale graphs. By dissecting state-of-the-art models, we identified a critical architectural limitation: agents evaluate the network globally without explicitly conditioning on the target node, while relying on static embeddings that fail to capture real-time topological changes during the rewiring process. In this paper, we introduce a novel DRL architecture designed to overcome these fundamental limitations. We propose an Actor-Critic system powered by Graph Attention Networks v2 (GATv2). By leveraging a target-aware feature set that combines static original-graph indicators with dynamically updated structural signals, and by explicitly contextualizing the target node through a dynamic attention mechanism, our model accurately represents the evolving graph state. Extensive experimental evaluation confirms that our architecture significantly outperforms existing baselines, achieving high hiding success rates with minimal structural perturbation and notable gains in computational efficiency.

title: From Problem-Structured QAOA to Problem-Agnostic Variational MaxCut Solvers: Representation, Redundancy, and Optimization Landscapes
abstract: Variational quantum optimization provides a useful setting for examining how circuit structure, parameterization, and trainability interact in practice. Objectives: Among the most promising variational quantum algorithms, the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) depends critically on circuit architecture, but greater circuit complexity does not necessarily lead to easier optimization or better solutions. Using the Maximum Cut (MaxCut) problem on graphs as a controlled setting, we investigate how variational behavior changes as problem-specific QAOA structure is progressively removed, with particular attention to representational capacity, optimization geometry, and finite-budget trainability. Methods: We analytically characterize a graph-agnostic product-state formulation of MaxCut and derive exact equivalences, redundancies, and local-landscape properties. These results motivate a controlled comparison among separable product ansätze, a representative graphagnostic entangling circuit, and graph-structured QAOA at several depths, including a parameter-count-matched control. The numerical benchmark comprises 95 small unweighted graph instances optimized under a common objective-evaluation budget. Results: The product-state formulation preserves the exact discrete MaxCut optimum, while its strict local maxima correspond to classical cuts that are stable under singlevertex flips. Redundant phase parameters increase optimization effort without enlarging the objective-relevant family. Under the prescribed optimization budget, the productstate ansatz attains higher average solution quality than the tested QAOA depths while requiring substantially fewer objective evaluations. The graph-agnostic entangling comparator provides no consistent advantage over the separable baseline, and a simple classical local-search method remains highly competitive. Conclusion: In the regime considered here, objective-relevant parameterization and optimization geometry can be as important as circuit richness.

title: SUN'IY YARATILGAN MATNLARNI ANIQLASHDA INVARIANTLAR VA DASTURIY FILTRLASH JARAYONI
abstract: Maqolada sun'iy yaratilgan matnlarni aniqlash algoritmini dasturiy filtrlash jarayoniga tatbiq etish masalasi ko'rib chiqiladi. Yondashuv matnni dastlabki tayyorlash, lingvistik-statistik xususiyatlarni hisoblash, xususiyatlar vektorini sinf invariantlari bilan taqqoslash va qaror ishonchliligini baholash bosqichlariga ajratiladi. Manbada keltirilgan tajriba jadvalidagi I va II tur xatoliklar ko'rsatkichlari tahlil qilinib, sinonimlash orqali yaratilgan matnlar uchun lug'at tanlovi xatolik darajasiga ta'sir qilishi ko'rsatiladi. Natijalar dasturiy filtrlashda faqat yakuniy yorliqni emas, balki qarorning ishonchlilik darajasi va xato xavfini ham hisobga olish kerakligini asoslaydi.

title: Where Multi-Step Reasoning Breaks: Measuring Error Propagation and Structured Scaffolds in Small Language Models
abstract: Chain-of-thought prompting lets a language model write out its intermediate reasoning, and a wrong intermediate claim can carry through to a wrong final answer. This preprint measures that error propagation directly for Qwen2.5-1.5B, Qwen2.5-3B and Llama-3.2-3B Instruct, run locally in 4-bit. On ProofWriter, every ground claim a model asserts is checked against the theory's full derivation closure. On GSM8K, every stated calculation is checked for arithmetic and against the intermediate values of the reference solution. The paper then asks whether structured scaffolds (explicit step decomposition, step-wise decoding with a self-verifier or an oracle verifier, and self-consistency) reduce step errors, their propagation, or both. Chains that contain a step error do end wrong more often, and the association survives adjustment for problem depth. Most wrong answers, though, contain no checkable step error. On ProofWriter they fail at the final inference about the queried statement, never state it, or give no answer. On GSM8K they compute the wrong quantity with correct arithmetic (0.628, 0.723 and 0.680 of wrong chain-of-thought chains for the three models). An oracle verifier that removes checkable step errors by construction does not beat chain-of-thought on either benchmark for either Qwen model, and a self-verifier does no better. Across eight model and benchmark cells, including FOLIO, structured decomposition is never measurably better than chain-of-thought, and self-consistency gives the only consistent gains, which are small. On GSM8K the oracle result holds under a second prompt wording. For models of this size, planning and the final inference are the bottleneck, and intermediate slips account for a minority of wrong answers. Preprint, not peer-reviewed. All models ran on a personal laptop and all datasets are public.

title: Sistema 3 (Poliedro Cognitivo) — Génesis de primitivas
abstract: Este notebook implementa el descubrimiento autónomo de primitivas matemáticas desde la ignorancia absoluta. Al prescindir de un diccionario humano con operaciones complejas predefinidas, el motor simbólico emplea exclusivamente axiomas rudimentarios (sucesión y predecesión). El agente optimiza la exploración algorítmica mediante el juez de Kolmogórov, respetando el principio de frugalidad cognitiva y cristalizando las nuevas topologías descubiertas.

title: Sequential RF Fingerprinting for AIS: Rejecting Unknown Vessels and Insider MMSI Spoofs Days After Enrollment
abstract: Any AIS transmitter can claim any vessel's identity (MMSI), because nothing in the protocol authenticates it; only the transmitter's analog hardware reveals who is really sending. We treat AIS traffic as streams of bursts keyed by claimed MMSI and accumulate physical-layer evidence with a sequential test. Each burst is scored by its k-nearest-neighbor distance to enrolled fingerprints in the feature space of a classifier whose weights are fixed after training, calibrated into a tail probability, and accumulated by a geometric-entropy-minimization cumulative-sum (GEM-CUSUM) statistic. The same test rejects unknown transmitters when scored against all enrolled vessels, and exposes insider spoofs when scored against the claimed vessel. A threshold refreshed from genuine traffic alone keeps it at a stated false-alarm rate as fingerprints drift. On AIS in-phase/quadrature (I/Q) recordings captured over 13 days at the Istanbul Strait (Bosphorus), the detector rejects unseen vessels at least 10 days after enrollment. Evaluated over 50-burst trials with every vessel weighted equally, it reaches an area under the ROC curve (AUROC) of 0.956 (95% confidence interval 0.913-0.989), where the best score computed from one burst at a time reaches 0.899. A threshold refreshed from the first quarter of the enrolled vessels' traffic holds 5.3% false alarms (3.0-9.2% across five independently trained encoders) at 88.8% detection. Scored against the claimed MMSI, enrolled transmitters spoofing another vessel are rejected at 0.991, a threat that open-set tests cannot see (AUROC 0.500, chance level). The lightweight Transformer GLFormer, reimplemented from its paper (no code is public) and retrained on the same data, reaches 0.652 in the same detector with its published in-phase input and 0.849 when given the same I/Q input as our encoder.

title: Conformalized Physics-Informed Weak Regression for Parameter Estimation in Epidemic Models
abstract: Compartment models of infectious diseases are often linear in coefficients that are physical parameters or products or ratios of them. We exploit this with closed-form least squares and equip the estimates with distribution-free uncertainty. Physics-informed regression (PIR) fits the parameters to finite-difference derivatives of the data; we introduce physics-informed weak regression (PIWR), which integrates the model in time instead, needs no derivatives of the data, estimates the initial state jointly and is high-order accurate. To quantify uncertainty we wrap both estimators in split conformal prediction, with a calibration population generated by the physics-based model itself, giving simultaneous intervals for all parameters with a finite-sample coverage guarantee. A residual-adaptive factor, computed without ground truth, scales the intervals to each data set (PIWR-RACC). On the eleven benchmark models of disease-informed neural networks (DINNs), PIWR or PIR-FD6 is one to four orders of magnitude more accurate than the reported DINN results wherever the sampling resolves the dynamics, in about a millisecond per fit instead of minutes to hours of training, and the 90% intervals achieve 87-92% coverage in all 88 settings. On the S3I3R model of the original PIR study, PIWR lowers the reported PIR errors by about three orders of magnitude. On real data from the 1978 boarding-school influenza outbreak, a variable-projection variant gives calibrated 95% intervals that overlap those of a Bayesian analysis. On a time-varying transmission benchmark, a B-spline expansion of beta(t) keeps PIR and PIWR linear; they are more accurate than physics-informed neural networks in three of four cases and comparable in the noisiest, with simultaneous bands for beta(t). The complete conformal calibration takes less than two minutes for every benchmark.

The complete conformal calibration takes less than two minutes for every benchmark.

title: Steertuning Policies from a Few Human Videos
abstract: Current recipes for robot learning require massive amounts of robot demonstrations to obtain robust and adaptive policies. In this work, we introduce Steertuning, a system that enables robots to learn new tasks in new environments from 5 human demonstrations in under 5 Steertuning consists of two parts. (1) We pretrain a 400M-parameter diffusion policy on our egocentric human dataset, which consists of 100 hours of densely annotated random interactions. This pretraining makes Steertuning robust to background differences and enables spatial and object generalization when deployed on new tasks. (2) Given 5 demonstrations of a new task, we finetune our model for only 2 minutes (2000 training updates) and steer the policy's actions during reverse sampling using the demonstration whose observation is closest to that of the deployment environment. Together with a carefully designed data processing pipeline for embodiment transfer, this enables Steertuning to achieve a 71% success rate across 12 tasks in 12 new environments, ranging from lab settings to kitchens in new homes. The entire process, from data collection for a new task to robot policy deployment, takes less than 5 minutes. Our full dataset, model weights, codebase, and robot videos will be made available at our website: https://steertuning.github.io.

title: Aligning Faithfulness for Theory-Scale Autoformalization
abstract: Autoformalization (AF) requires more than compilation: formal statements must preserve the meaning of their informal sources, a property known as faithfulness. An emerging frontier is the automated evaluation of this property, yet most existing methods operate at the statement level and produce whole-item verdicts, failing to reveal how individual expressions correspond or which contextual interpretations support the judgment. This omission is consequential because AF is inherently theory-scale: target statements derive their meaning from surrounding mathematical material and unstated conventions. We formulate faithfulness evaluation as a context-aware align-then-label problem: identifying phrase-level correspondences between informal and formal statements and assigning a faithfulness label to each under explicitly specified contextual interpretations and assumptions. We also introduce FaithAlign, the first theory-scale faithfulness benchmark comprising 460 items and 4,982 annotated phrase-level links, alongside FaithAlign-Gap, a companion set of 146 items with informal context and assumptions withheld. Each FaithAlign item includes the target statement pair, relevant context, formal dependencies, and, where needed, assumptions specifying one given interpretation. Across 8 models, GPT-6 Astra achieves the highest defect F1 at 47.8% and identifies all defects in only 4.5% of items with two or more defects. On FaithAlign-Gap, Astra identifies only 28.2% of undecidable items as such. These results show the difficulty of recovering context-dependent correspondences, establishing FaithAlign as a testbed for fine-grained, context-aware faithfulness evaluation.

title: Holding Agents Accountable with Verifiable Agent Insurance
abstract: While AI agents are useful for many tasks, they regularly misbehave in destructive ways, such as deleting important data. While prior work has focused on preventing such misbehavior, we consider how to recover after an agent misbehaves. We propose verifiable agent insurance (VAI), a framework for agent providers to commit financially to promises, a list of programmatically-specified policies that an agent is meant to follow. These promises are embedded in a smart contract on an immutable ledger (e.g., a blockchain) to prevent tampering, along with a monetary escrow. A user who detects a violation of committed promises can prompt a verifier to review agent execution traces, which are logged through the agent harness's shared tool-execution path, without instrumenting each tool separately. Upon verification of the violation, the agent provider's escrow funds are paid to the reporting user. We instantiate VAI as an end-to-end implementation on an Ethereum layer-2 network, and evaluate its coverage on three prominent agent benchmarks, two of which we re-annotated to obtain task-level policy-compliance labels. Currently, many agents do not emit user authorizations and security-relevant information as explicit, structured data objects -- rather, they embed the data needed to verify policy violations in natural language exchanges. Even so, VAI manages to detect violations in 42.2% of runs containing violations across three benchmarks. By augmenting agents to explicitly emit such objects, violation detection rises to 83.0% of traces. Our findings suggest that for improved auditability, agents should be co-designed with their security policies to emit explicit, structured records of user authorization and security-relevant actions.

title: Exact power indices for plurality-voting ensembles
abstract: Plurality-voting ensembles aggregate the predictions of multiple base classifiers and output the most voted class, with ties typically broken at random. Despite the simple aggregation rule, attributing the impact of each base classifier to the ensemble's predictions is far from straightforward. That is, a single base classifier's impact depends on how it interacts with the votes of all other classifiers in the ensemble, for example, in resolving ties, and not only on its own predictions. We address the attribution problem using established tools from cooperative game theory, studying the Banzhaf and Shapley power indices for new games modeling plurality voting and random tie-breaking, for binary and multiclass classification settings. Computing power indices is, in general, intractable. Surprisingly, our methods, collectively named ENPOWER, enable the exact computation of Banzhaf and Shapley values in linear time for the binary classification setting and in low-degree polynomial time for the multiclass setting. The algorithms in ENPOWER rely on new combinatorial formulations of the Banzhaf and Shapley indices, yielding closed-form solutions for the binary case and ordinary generating function representations for the multiclass case. We validate empirically the methods in ENPOWER demonstrating their high applicability, providing attribution values not captured by existing methods. We apply the attribution of ENPOWER to: ensemble pruning and prompt-based ensembling of vision-language models.

title: YUBI-Real2Sim: 3DGS Scene Verification for Reliable Policy Evaluation
abstract: Evaluating VLA policies on real robots is costly, time-consuming, and difficult to reproduce, making real-to-sim simulation essential for scalable evaluation. While 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) enables rapid real-to-sim scene generation, the reconstruction quality required for reliable policy evaluation remains unquantified. In particular, policies relying on wrist-mounted fisheye cameras (e.g., YUBI handheld gripper data) are heavily exposed to visual artifacts (holes, floaters) in wide-angle views, directly degrading task performance. To address this, we present YUBI-Real2Sim, a unified framework for 3DGS-based scene reconstruction and real-to-sim policy evaluation under dual fisheye wrist views. We develop an integrated pipeline combining 200-degree fisheye camera capture, 3DGS training, 3D foundation models for object modeling, and MuJoCo-based physical simulation, reproducing the observed real-world policy ordering in eight of nine scene-task comparisons. Using this framework, we construct a benchmark across two bimanual robot platforms, three scenes, three tasks, and dual pi0.5-based policies. This systematically measures real-to-sim rank agreement and evaluates policy sensitivity against counterfactual 3DGS artifacts (ceiling holes, floaters, warping) and capture disturbances. We further analyze whether novel-view quality scores can indicate policy-ranking reliability under a scene-held-out evaluation protocol. The results show task-dependent performance and limitations of quality-based reliability prediction, highlighting the need to assess reconstruction quality when using Real2Sim for policy evaluation. These results do not yet establish a generally reliable scene-acceptance rule. Project Page: https://yubi-real2sim.airoa.io.

title: Desarrollo de un prototipo para bloquear contenido abusivo en plataformas educativas en línea– contexto Escuela Politécnica Nacional: extensión de seguridad y monitoreo de contenido.
abstract: El incremento de interacciones en plataformas educativas virtuales expone a estudiantes y docentes a mensajes con contenido abusivo, mientras las instituciones no siempre disponen de control directo sobre la infraestructura de dichas plataformas. Ante este problema, el proyecto tiene como objetivo desarrollar un mecanismo seguro para capturar, monitorear, registrar y visualizar entradas de texto, integrado con un sistema de clasificación basado en inteligencia artificial, para detectar y notificar oportunamente contenido potencialmente abusivo. Metodológicamente, se aplicó un enfoque incremental e iterativo orientado a la integración de componentes reales. Se implementó una extensión de navegador en Manifest V3 que identificó campos de entrada en dominios educativos, detectó el momento de envío del mensaje y remitió el texto cifrado mediante AES a un servidor local Flask. Una vez que el servidor descifró los datos, estos fueron procesados por un modelo Transformer local que los evaluó bajo cuatro categorías (No Offensive, Humor and Offensive Comments, Intoleran ce y Violence) para así calcular el nivel de riesgo. Con este resultado en mano, la extensión generó las notificaciones para el usuario y almacenó los registros a nivel local.Esto permitió llevar un registro de las consultas y exportar los datos a Excel, quedando todas las activi dades guardadas en una base de datos SQLite para temas de auditoría. Como medida de contención, la extensión bloqueó el dominio infractor apoyándose en la API declarativeNe tRequest. Esta restricción de red se diseñó de forma reversible, dejando que el usuario la levantara directamente desde la interfaz gráfica si lo consideraba necesario. Las pruebas funcionales confirmaron que la integración de los componentes fue exitosa al validar que todo el flujo de captura, clasificación, registro y mitigación operara sin contratiempos en el entorno del prototipo

title: QUANTUM COHERENCE PRESERVING NANOFABRICATION PROCESS WINDOWS AT THE LIMIT Research Architecture Edition v1.0 | STARLI / White Rainbow Civilization ABSTRACT This research architecture examines a testable and deliberately platform-specific question: under which nanofabrication conditions do deposition, lithography, etching, annealing, bonding, cleaning, and other energy-bearing operations satisfy nanoscale geometric tolerances while also preserving relevant quantum function? The central proposal is to qualify fabrication through joint, conditional observations of process state, surface and interface defects, electrical and thermal behavior, and device-specific measurements of coherence, noise, spectroscopy, or photonic performance. Geometry-only yield and aesthetic micrographs are not accepted as proxies for coherence. The monograph treats process qualification as an observationally defined joint event rather than a product of assumed-independent success probabilities. For superconducting circuits, plausible contributors include dielectric two-level-system losses, Purcell channels, nonequilibrium quasiparticles, magnetic defects, and packaging effects. For silicon spin qubits, charge traps, valley splitting, interface disorder, magnetic noise, and control geometry may require different characterization and validation protocols. The proposed framework does not assume that one recipe or coherence metric generalizes across quantum platforms. RESEARCH DESIGN Five research layers structure the inquiry: (1) fabrication-energy and material-state provenance; (2) joint nanoscale, defect, classical-electrical, and quantum-function metrology; (3) conditional acceptance modeling and uncertainty; (4) wafer, apparatus, operator, and material-lot shift tests; and (5) independent blind reproduction and responsible handover. A particularly important possible outcome is a null result: if mature classical metrology predicts final quantum device failure as well as a quantum-aware model, the more elaborate process-window hypothesis is rejected. SCOPE OF THIS EDITION This architecture edition comprises 82 chapters and 410 individually paginated research sections, 30 introductory physics/statistics derivation plates, 200 Research Gates that specify falsifiable experiments, 33 Phoenix Answer Embryos as provisional and revisable design proposals, and 233 indexed equation signposts combining a physical reference with a separately defined research diagnostic. It includes references to established materials-loss and semiconductor-spin-qubit literature and a clear distinction among known physics, engineering models, and untested hypotheses. IMPORTANT SCIENTIFIC AND EDITORIAL LIMITATIONS This is a research architecture, not a report of experiments newly performed for the book and not an independent certification of coherence-preserving process settings. The 233 signposts are 233 indexed composite expressions, not 233 newly discovered independent physical laws. Physical anchor formulas recur where applicable, and model applicability must be checked in every proposed study. The manuscript has not yet met the separately specified 200,000-word substantive-English target: the current paragraph-level count is approximately 121,000 English words, with methodological scaffolds still requiring independent source-rich development. Therefore the edition should not be advertised as a completed 200K+ research monograph. SOURCE LINEAGE The concept extends the author-provided NANO_QUANTUM_FISSION_18_FRONTIER_RESEARCH_FLAGSHIPS v2.0 architecture and identifies Q3 (swarm assembly of quantum devices), Q7 (AI closed-loop quantum-nanofabrication), and Q8 (stigmergic swarm manufacturing under measurement uncertainty) as conceptual mother frameworks. These chapter references are research lineage pointers and do not validate the proposed cross-domain integration. The monograph treats process qualification as an observationally defined joint event rather than a product of assumed-independent success probabilities. For superconducting circuits, plausible contributors include dielectric two-level-system losses, Purcell channels, nonequilibrium quasiparticles, magnetic defects, and packaging effects. For silicon spin qubits, charge traps, valley splitting, interface disorder, magnetic noise, and control geometry may require different characterization and validation protocols. The proposed framework does not assume that one recipe or coherence metric generalizes across quantum platforms. RESEARCH DESIGN Five research layers structure the inquiry: (1) fabrication-energy and material-state provenance; (2) joint nanoscale, defect, classical-electrical, and quantum-function metrology; (3) conditional acceptance modeling and uncertainty; (4) wafer, apparatus, operator, and material-lot shift tests; and (5) independent blind reproduction and responsible handover. A particularly important possible outcome is a null result: if mature classical metrology predicts final quantum device failure as well as a quantum-aware model, the more elaborate process-window hypothesis is rejected. SCOPE OF THIS EDITION This architecture edition comprises 82 chapters and 410 individually paginated research sections, 30 introductory physics/statistics derivation plates, 200 Research Gates that specify falsifiable experiments, 33 Phoenix Answer Embryos as provisional and revisable design proposals, and 233 indexed equation signposts combining a physical reference with a separately defined research diagnostic. It includes references to established materials-loss and semiconductor-spin-qubit literature and a clear distinction among known physics, engineering models, and untested hypotheses. IMPORTANT SCIENTIFIC AND EDITORIAL LIMITATIONS This is a research architecture, not a report of experiments newly performed for the book and not an independent certification of coherence-preserving process settings. The 233 signposts are 233 indexed composite expressions, not 233 newly discovered independent physical laws. Physical anchor formulas recur where applicable, and model applicability must be checked in every proposed study. The manuscript has not yet met the separately specified 200,000-word substantive-English target: the current paragraph-level count is approximately 121,000 English words, with methodological scaffolds still requiring independent source-rich development. Therefore the edition should not be advertised as a completed 200K+ research monograph. SOURCE LINEAGE The concept extends the author-provided NANO_QUANTUM_FISSION_18_FRONTIER_RESEARCH_FLAGSHIPS v2.0 architecture and identifies Q3 (swarm assembly of quantum devices), Q7 (AI closed-loop quantum-nanofabrication), and Q8 (stigmergic swarm manufacturing under measurement uncertainty) as conceptual mother frameworks. These chapter references are research lineage pointers and do not validate the proposed cross-domain integration. title: GRLoRA v2.1 - run records, dataset manifests and figures for the conflict-diagnosis and leakage-controlled educational multi-task benchmark study
abstract: Run records, dataset manifests and figures accompanying the study Diagnosing Conflict-Mitigation Regularizers in Multi-Task Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning: A Leakage-Controlled Educational Benchmark and an Evaluation Protocol. Contents. results/ per-run run_config.json, training_log.jsonl and val_metrics.json, plus summary tables for the 12-point lambda grid, the component-isolation runs and the three-seed confirmation. logs/ raw launcher stdout and exit codes. manifests/ dataset_manifest_v2_1.json (SHA-256 of every upstream and processed file), the data readiness gates, the de-duplication report and per-task build statistics. samples/ first 10 rows of every split, for schema documentation only. reports/ data sources, data audits, the pre-registered lambda calibration protocol and the implementation-guard reports. figure_data/ tidy CSVs extracted from the run artifacts. figures/ the seven manuscript figures (PDF + PNG) and the rendered text-collision audit. Provenance. Every processed split carries a SHA-256 in dataset_manifest_v2_1.json (manifest digest d68d4a87e3ccda21ae2215263805e10fabd075162b30553847e5542ca7ad4164) and every run records the data-manifest hash it was trained against, so any run can be tied to an exact data revision. Upstream data. The benchmark is derived from three public corpora: MathDial (CC BY 4.0), the Atomi HuggingFace mirror of SemEval-2013 Task 7 (beetle 5-way), and OULAD (CC BY 4.0, DOI 10.24432/C5KK69). Per-file SHA-256 for every downloaded upstream file is recorded in the manifest. The processed splits are not redistributed; they are reproducible from the deposited construction scripts and verifiable against the recorded hashes (see DATA_LICENSES.md). Scope. The three-seed confirmation covers lambda_orth = 0.001; lambda_orth = 0.01 and 0.1 were run at seed 42 only. Every reported number is a validation-split number; the test partition was not accessed.

title: Deep Generative Models for Phylogenetic Inference with Complex Evolutionary Processes
abstract: Inference of phylogenetic trees from sequences plays a central role in understanding evolutionary relationships, with applications ranging from tracking pathogen spread to reconstructing the history of life. Conventionally, practitioners obtain posteriors over trees using likelihood-based methods like MCMC. However, likelihoods are only available for simple evolutionary models with restrictive assumptions. For realistic evolutionary models, inference using conventional methods is prohibitively expensive, inaccurate, or even impossible. In practice, practitioners settle for using as flexible a conventional method as possible, even though they expect it is misspecified. In principle, we could use simulation-based inference: simulate tree and sequence data from an evolutionary model and train a neural network to predict the posterior over trees given sequences. However it is a mathematical challenge to represent and train complex posterior distributions over trees. Here we present a flexible family of conditional generative models over trees. Our models iteratively build trees using three natural paradigms -- top-down, middle-out, or bottom-up -- and are trained using a discrete diffusion framework. For real and synthetic datasets of up to $65$ taxa and $>10^5$ tokens, our models recover MCMC posteriors much more accurately than the previous state-of-the-art simulation-based method Phyloformer 2. Finally, we compare to IQ-Tree, a popular flexible-but-misspecified conventional method. Our models match its tree estimates on simple data, but on more realistic data, our method is reliably more accurate.

title: Seeing Depth but Choosing Cues in Vision-Language Models
abstract: Do vision-language models use depth information to judge which object is closer, or rely on image-plane cues? We investigate this question through controlled depth--cue conflicts, representation analysis, and interventions. Among the many image-plane cues relevant to depth perception, we focus on apparent size and vertical position. We compare depth judgments under cue-consistent and cue-conflict conditions in both rendered scenes and real-world photographs. Across model families and scales, depth judgments systematically shift toward misleading cues. Yet the correct depth order remains decodable from the queried objects' visual representations, including when the model answers incorrectly. Image and category controls support interpreting this signal as image-dependent depth information beyond the two target cues. Strengthening the model's own depth readout through object-level write-back can correct conflict decisions without updating model parameters or using ground-truth depth annotations. Interventions show that the effect of this correction depends on the direction and target tokens of the written signal, while its strength varies across architectures and domains. Together, these findings reveal a mismatch between a model's ability to represent depth and use this information when deciding the answer. VLMs can retain useful depth information while allowing competing image-plane cues to exert greater influence on their answers.

title: HiSTOR: Structured Treatment-outcome Representation Learning for High-Dimensional Longitudinal Data
abstract: Estimating potential outcomes under alternative treatment sequences is essential for personalized decision-making, but remains challenging with high-dimensional covariates and time-varying confounding. In this study, we propose HiSTOR (High-dimensional Structured Treatment-Outcome Representation), an end-to-end framework that integrates nonlinear dimension reduction with longitudinal counterfactual prediction. The central idea is to learn structured low-dimensional representations of both current patient states and evolving histories, according to their shared and distinct relationships with treatment assignment and outcomes. This extends latent-space covariate adjustment to longitudinal settings, jointly addressing covariate dimensionality and historical complexity. The resulting framework supports one-step and multi-step outcome prediction under specified treatment sequences. Experiments on CVSim and CancerSim demonstrate the superiority of HiSTOR across varying covariate dimensions, confounding strengths, and prediction horizons compared to state-of-the-art methods. To sum up, HiSTOR offers a unified approach to connecting high-dimensional covariate adjustment with longitudinal potential-outcome prediction.

title: Gaussian Splatting for Real-Time Scene Reconstruction: Methods, Systems, and Trade-offs
abstract: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) allows for high-quality real-time novel-view synthesis. Since its inception in 2023, its explicit and highly configurable scene representation has been extended toward sparse-view generation, dynamic reconstruction, efficiency and compression, streaming, and simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM). Although Gaussian Splatting can provide real-time rendering, rendering an existing representation is distinct from constructing, updating, or maintaining the scene itself. In this survey, we synthesize current literature, categorize them and provide a connection of current approaches and tools towards an end-to-end pipeline. Explicitly, we categorize GS scene reconstruction into five overlapping families: single-shot generation, dynamic representations, efficiency and compression, streaming and immersive systems, and Gaussian Splatting SLAM. We distinguish render-only throughput from task-specific scene generation, update, tracking, mapping, and optimization costs, and combine controlled sparse-view benchmarking with native evaluations to identify cross-family quality, latency, memory, and update-cost trade-offs.

title: Experimental Evaluation of Retrieval Strategies in RAG Architectures Applied to the Judicial Domain
abstract: Este trabajo presenta el diseño, implementación y evaluación experimental de un sistema Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) aplicado al dominio judicial penal. El objetivo principal fue analizar el desempeño del componente de recuperación semántica en un entorno completamente local, seguro y reproducible, utilizando un corpus real compuesto por 2.592 sentencias judiciales y 46.382 fragmentos vectorizados. El pipeline implementado integra segmentación textual mediante Recursive Character Text Splitter, embeddings densos generados con all-mpnet-base-v2, almacenamiento en ChromaDB y generación contextual con un modelo LLM ejecutado localmente. La evaluación se centró exclusivamente en el módulo de retrieval, empleando métricas estándar de Information Retrieval como Precision@5 y Mean Reciprocal Rank (MRR), complementadas con análisis de similitud coseno y evaluación manual experta de relevancia. Los resultados muestran alta coherencia temática en la recuperación, pero limitaciones en la discriminación de fundamentos jurídicos específicos, especialmente ante variaciones lingüísticas en las consultas. Se identifican como líneas de mejora la incorporación de embeddings jurídicos especializados, técnicas de re-ranking con cross-encoders y optimización del esquema de chunking. El estudio aporta evidencia empírica sobre los desafíos estructurales de los sistemas RAG jurídicos y establece un baseline reproducible para investigaciones futuras.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Economic and Financial Communication: Challenges, Practices, and Perspectives for More Transparent and Efficient Information
abstract: In a context of accelerated digital transformation, this article examines the extent to which and the conditions under which artificial intelligence (AI) transforms economic and financial communication by improving information quality, transparency, and decision-making efficiency. Drawing on agency theory, information asymmetry, and information governance, it proposes a conceptual model articulating a chain of relationships whereby AI influences information quality, which in turn shapes transparency, ultimately improving decision-making performance, while also integrating a direct effect of AI on that performance and a risk of algorithmic opacity. The model further incorporates moderating variables: information governance arrangements, data quality, and the complementarity between human expertise and intelligent systems, resulting in eight research hypotheses covering both direct and moderating effects across the model. An exploratory qualitative study, based on semi-structured interviews with twenty-three professionals from the public and private sectors, conducted either in person or remotely and processed through thematic analysis, shows that AI is predominantly perceived as a lever for automation, reliability, and decision support, particularly through the reduction of human errors and the processing of massive data volumes. However, these effects remain conditional upon the quality of input data, adequate governance arrangements, and the maintenance of human oversight, while risks of algorithmic opacity, bias, hallucinations, and confidentiality persist, alongside a structural lag in adoption within the public sector. The article therefore supports a contingent, non-techno-deterministic understanding of AI in economic and financial communication, in which technological value added remains subordinate to data quality, governance, and human intervention rather than to the technology itself.

title: Code and raw results for "Hyperparameter Advisors Built on Three LLMs Did Not Beat Default-Seeded TPE on Small Tabular Tasks"
abstract: Code, protocols and every raw result behind the article "Hyperparameter Advisors Built on Three LLMs Did Not Beat Default-Seeded TPE on Small Tabular Tasks: Four of 15 Pre-Specified Hypothesis Tests Passed, and the Comparison Depends on TPE's Start-Up Trials" (Rodrigues, Vas, DCosta and Prabhakaran; under submission). The archive holds the benchmark harness (search space and default configuration, seeded classical optimizers, the LLM advisor prompts and loop), the protocols and dated amendments written before each run, the run scripts, every raw result analysed in the article (including every raw LLM request and response of the fresh suite for Claude Haiku 4.5, GPT-4.1 mini and Llama 3.3 70B Instruct, the units discarded after failed calls, and every rerun of the TPE start-up check), and the analysis scripts that regenerate every number, table and figure from the stored files. All datasets are public PMLB benchmarks, fetched by the included loader. To regenerate the article's numbers: cd mlj-revision-2026-10-12 && P04_MS=draft-asc python3 analyze.py, then cd startup-sensitivity-2026-10-13 && python3 analyze_startup.py --out ../draft-asc. The analysis reproduces every digit from the stored results; re-running the optimizers on other hardware reproduces the conclusions but CV accuracy can differ by a few tenths of a point. See SUPPLEMENT-README in the archive for the layout and software versions. An earlier version of this work, with a different title and claims, is arXiv:2606.21641.

title: How Forms Become Reconstructible: Acquired Records, Reciprocal Repair, and Functional Renewal
abstract: How can a pattern or learned response be rebuilt after damage or replacement? Using computer models, we distinguish what past experience leaves behind, what a system does now, and what a replacement can recover. We call the information carried forward a record, and test how systems use it and write a new one. In spatial models, records of patterns formed without a supplied target image help later systems recover features specific to the original pattern. This modest effect persists through sixteen replacements, even as measured reconstruction becomes less accurate. Surviving organization in a damaged system can improve a record's usefulness to a new system. An exploratory follow-up finds that capturing surviving activity early can partly restore a distinction removed from the record. Changing how that record is read or rewritten also changes what is rebuilt. In a separate network model, one of two simple taught response rules can be recovered after 32 damaged rebuilds, despite failures along the way. Success depends on different record features under different rebuilding conditions. A repair procedure fixed before testing raises success in a fresh reconstruction from 81.52% to 87.45%. In a separate experiment, repair at every rebuild raises the proportion succeeding throughout eighteen rebuilds from 77.54% to 89.84%. In a model of communicating cells, cells sharing the same coarse regulatory classification differ in their ability to pass that state to replacements. Changing specific internal components or communication timing changes this ability. Rebuilding can restore function after specified losses, but preserving a record unchanged often works better. Some successes remain sensitive to numerical details, and better forecasts do not always yield better repair choices. The central finding is that retaining information, expressing it now, and using it to rebuild later are different capacities. The models provide controlled ways to study these differences; a general predictive theory, inherited flexible problem-solving and validation in living systems remain open.

evidence.title: How Forms Become Reconstructible: Acquired Records, Reciprocal Repair, and Functional Renewal
evidence.abstract: How can a pattern or learned response be rebuilt after damage or replacement? Using computer models, we distinguish what past experience leaves behind, what a system does now, and what a replacement can recover. We call the information carried forward a record, and test how systems use it and write a new one. In spatial models, records of patterns formed without a supplied target image help later systems recover features specific to the original pattern. This modest effect persists through sixteen replacements, even as measured reconstruction becomes less accurate. Surviving organization in a damaged system can improve a record's usefulness to a new system. An exploratory follow-up finds that capturing surviving activity early can partly restore a distinction removed from the record. Changing how that record is read or rewritten also changes what is rebuilt. In a separate network model, one of two simple taught response rules can be recovered after 32 damaged rebuilds, despite failures along the way. Success depends on different record features under different rebuilding conditions. A repair procedure fixed before testing raises success in a fresh reconstruction from 81.52% to 87.45%. In a separate experiment, repair at every rebuild raises the proportion succeeding throughout eighteen rebuilds from 77.54% to 89.84%. In a model of communicating cells, cells sharing the same coarse regulatory classification differ in their ability to pass that state to replacements. Changing specific internal components or communication timing changes this ability. Rebuilding can restore function after specified losses, but preserving a record unchanged often works better. Some successes remain sensitive to numerical details, and better forecasts do not always yield better repair choices. The central finding is that retaining information, expressing it now, and using it to rebuild later are different capacities. The models provide controlled ways to study these differences; a general predictive theory, inherited flexible problem-solving and validation in living systems remain open.

title: Short-Term Photovoltaic Power Forecasting Based on a CEEMDAN-PE-ISSA-TCN-Transformer Framework
abstract: This study proposes a CEEMDAN-PE-ISSA-TCN-Transformer framework for short-term photovoltaic (PV) power forecasting. Six pre-specified meteorological variables were retained, and their Pearson correlation coefficients with PV power were calculated using the training interval only. The power sequence was decomposed into high-frequency, medium-frequency, and low-frequency reconstructed components using CEEMDAN and permutation entropy (PE). A branch-specific residual TCN-self-attention forecasting network was constructed for each component, and an improved sparrow search algorithm (ISSA) was used to optimize the number of filters, the number of attention heads, and the initial learning rate. Four seasonal datasets, each containing 10 consecutive days of five-minute observations, were divided chronologically into training, validation, and untouched test intervals in a 7:1:2 ratio. For validation and test forecast origins, CEEMDAN used only the most recent 288 available historical power observations. Across the four within-season test intervals, the proposed model obtained RMSE values of 0.5905, 0.9661, 1.0645, and 1.2476; MAE values of 0.4434, 0.4796, 0.9104, and 0.7066; R2 values of 0.9631, 0.8499, 0.8819, and 0.8401; and WAPE values of 16.98%, 25.27%, 34.48%, and 26.78% in spring, summer, autumn, and winter, respectively. The results indicate improved point-forecast accuracy for the evaluated within-season configurations.

title: Data-free Multistep Diffusion Distillation
abstract: One-step diffusion distillation achieves strong performance on small datasets but remains insufficient for high-resolution or complex text-to-image settings. Extending to multistep distillation often requires training data, suffers from early-step degradation, inconsistent outputs across sampling budgets, and incurs high computational cost. We identify that these limitations stem from simultaneous training, where a single adapted network approximates multiple score functions of different student distributions at once, causing biased distribution matching and unstable optimization. Therefore, we propose Progressive Multistep Data-free Distillation (PMDD), which assigns a dedicated adapted network per student distribution while avoiding the memory overhead of maintaining multiple adapted networks. Combined with a stage-wise unforget loss to preserve earlier-step generations, PMDD reduces optimization bias in the student, provides faster convergence, and a single unified model that supports multiple inference budgets. Extensive experiments show that PMDD matches or outperforms data-free few-step baselines at every multistep budget, reaches FID 1.99 on ImageNet 64x64 in two steps, below its 512-NFE teacher (2.32), and achieves FID 7.76 on zero-shot COCO 512x512, while requiring 4-5x less training compute than data-free DMDv2 to support three inference budgets.

title: Why Do VLMs Fail at Remote Physiological Measurement? Rethinking with Physiological Grounding and Numerical Alignment
abstract: Video-based remote physiological measurement (RPM) has broad applications, while Vision-Language Models (VLMs) provide a promising opportunity to enable end-to-end physiological monitoring for future human-aware intelligent systems. However, existing RPM methods rely on task-specific models and cannot be seamlessly integrated with the multimodal understanding and interaction capabilities of VLMs. We revisit RPM with VLMs and provide empirical evidence for two major bottlenecks: generic visual semantic representations fail to preserve fine-grained physiological cues; while discrete token prediction in autoregressive generation is inherently misaligned with continuous numerical measurement. To address these challenges, we propose VITAL (Visual-physiological Token Alignment for Language Models), a visual-physiological token alignment framework for RPM and preserving general vision tasks. VITAL retains the original visual pathway for semantic understanding and introduces an independent physiological pathway to jointly model semantic and physiological information. Moreover, we propose a structured numerical alignment approach to improve the reliability of generative heart rate estimation by enhancing numerical relationship modeling. Extensive experiments show that VITAL improves cross-domain estimation performance on multiple rPPG datasets while preserving the general visual understanding capability of VLMs, demonstrating its effectiveness as a unified visual-physiological model. Code will be released.

title: All-electron machine-learned orbital-free density functional for periodic CHNO systems
abstract: We introduce STRUCTURES-P, a machine-learned all-electron orbital-free density functional for periodic CHNO systems. Electrostatics are evaluated analytically in an atom-centered Gaussian basis, while an equivariant network learns the kinetic and exchange-correlation energy from energies and gradients of non-ground-state densities. Minimizing the functional from a superposition of atomic densities recovers the Kohn-Sham ground state: on held-out crystals, the density error falls from 6.7% to 0.4% of the electron count and the energy error reaches 0.25 mHa per atom, half that of a same-architecture interatomic potential. A single functional can be trained for both isolated molecules and periodic systems, and the model generalizes to larger unit cells. It largely preserves relative-energy rankings and reproduces convex-hull vertices on the tested H-N composition slice. Together, these results demonstrate the viability of machine-learned all-electron orbital-free DFT for variational density optimization and energy evaluation in fixed-geometry solids.

title: Sobre los límites estructurales de los sistemas de decisión mediante aprendizaje automático: una perspectiva desde la teoría de la información, las interacciones y la dinámica estocástica
abstract: Machine learning procedures are commonly evaluated in terms of predictive accuracy and computational efficiency. However, their achievable performance is fundamentally constrained by structural properties of the underlying data-generating process, which are formalized in terms of informational bounds. In this work we examine intrinsic limits of datadriven decision systems from an information-theoretic and interactionbased perspective. We analyze minimal achievable error in classification through Fano-type bounds and precision limits in parametric estimation via the Cramér-Rao inequality, emphasizing that such limits depend on the underlying model rather than on algorithmic sophistication alone. We further discuss how implicit assumptions, such as independence, ergodicity, and distributional stability, affect the validity of inferential procedures. Building on interaction-based modeling principles, we review typical frameworks such as Markov Random Fields and potentialbased representations for encoding dependence mechanisms. We also describe decision systems, including LLM-integrated agent architectures, as feedback-driven stochastic processes where state-dependent dynamics may induce emergent macroscopic behavior. This perspective highlights the importance of having adequate models for the data as a prerequisite for expanding predictive capability, and situates algorithmic learning within the informational limits imposed by the models.

title: Стандартът ISO 21127:2023 Information and Documentation – A Reference Ontology for the Interchange of Cultural Heritage Information и достъпа до културното наследство
abstract: Статията разглежда ISO 21127:2023, международен стандарт, който предоставя референтна онтология за обмен на информация за културното наследство между архиви, библиотеки и музеи. Стандартът дефинира концептуални класове, свойства и връзки, осигуряващи семантична оперативна съвместимост между различни информационни системи и улеснява интеграцията на данни от институти на паметта. Той поддържа модели за машинно четене чрез RDF и OWL, позволява глобално търсене и извличане на знания, подпомага научна интерпретация и дигитализация на ресурси. ISO 21127:2023 служи като общ език за експерти и ИТ разработчици, предоставя добри практики за концептуално моделиране и обмен на културни данни.

title: Evaluasi Kompresi Lossless Huffman Statis pada Sampel Teks dan Citra Komik
abstract: Webtoon is a digital comic platform that presents stories as images and text on Android devices. Large files can increase storage requirements and slow access to content. This study aims to apply Huffman coding to reduce the size of text and image data obtained from comics on the Webtoon application. The method consists of counting symbol frequencies, creating a priority queue, constructing a Huffman tree, assigning binary codes, and replacing the original symbols with the resulting codes. Frequently occurring symbols receive shorter codes, whereas less frequent symbols receive longer codes. The algorithm was implemented in the Python programming language. Evaluation was performed by comparing data sizes before and after compression and calculating the percentage reduction. Text data decreased from 616 bits to 189 bits, while image data decreased from 512 bits to 380 bits. The manuscript reports compression percentages of 69.4% for text and 25.7% for images. These findings indicate that Huffman coding can reduce storage requirements for the data examined. The generated Huffman tree provides the basis for reconstructing the original data during decompression. Applying this method may support more efficient storage and transmission of digital comic content. Further research is recommended to evaluate combinations of Huffman coding with other compression methods and test performance across different user devices, particularly regarding image quality and application response time.

title: Semanturgie: Referenzen, Kodierung und kontrollierte Interpretation. Band 1 - Bedeutungssysteme, Datenmodelle und überprüfbare Übergänge
abstract: Konzeptionelles Terminologiewerk mit 200 deutsch-englischen Arbeitsdefinitionen in zehn Modulen. Beispiele, Gegenfälle und Grenzen stehen auf Deutsch. 102 Einträge formulieren allgemeine Fachkonzepte, 84 kennzeichnen Bereichsfestlegungen und 14 sind vorgeschlagene Präzisierungen. Die Module behandeln Bedeutungsbezug, RDF-Struktur, Literale und Werte, JSON-LD-Kontexte, Ontologieaxiome, SHACL-Validierung, Mappings, Transformation, Qualitätsgrenzen und kontrollierte Revision. Drei ausgearbeitete Gedankenfälle trennen Literalidentität und Wertgleichheit, OWL-Folgerung und SHACL-Prüfung sowie Kurzform und Kontextfassung. Öffentliche Quellen und tatsächliche Lesetiefe sind ausgewiesen. Die Definitionen sind eigene redaktionelle Arbeitsformulierungen. Historische Neuheit, universelle Bedeutungsgesetze, Normkonformität, unabhängige Fachbegutachtung und empirisch nachgewiesene Leistungssteigerung werden nicht beansprucht. Conceptual terminology volume containing 200 paired German-English working definitions. Constructed examples, counterexamples, and boundaries are in German. It identifies 102 general domain concepts, 84 scoped stipulations, and 14 proposed refinements. Ten modules cover meaning and reference, RDF structure, literals, JSON-LD contexts, ontology axioms, SHACL validation, mappings, transformations, quality boundaries, and controlled revision. Three developed thought cases separate literal identity from value equality, OWL entailment from SHACL validation, and shorthand from context version. Sources and actual reading scope are stated. No claim of historical novelty, universal laws of meaning, standards conformity, independent peer review, or empirically demonstrated performance improvement. PDF and TXT present the same text. Definitions and references are additionally supplied in JSON.

title: EL-RAKHAWI SYSTEM FOR THERMODYNAMIC DEEP LEARNING WITH MINIMAL ENERGY DISSIPATION (TDL-MED) Invention Disclosure Document & Technical Whitepaper
abstract: TDL-MED: THERMODYNAMIC DEEP LEARNING WITH MINIMAL ENERGY DISSIPATION Author: Dr. Mohamed Kamal Arafa El-RakhawiDOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23333980 An energy-efficient neural network training framework achieving 60-80% reduction in computational dissipation through Thermodynamic Gradient Descent (TGD). Core innovation: constrained optimization minimizing information-geometric entropy production σ_update = Σ(Δθ_i)²/τ_i subject to target loss reduction ε. Update rule: Δθ_i = -ε τ_i (∂L/∂θ_i) / Σ_j τ_j (∂L/∂θ_j)². Timescales τ_i inversely proportional to local curvature via stochastic diagonal Hessian estimation (Hutchinson's estimator with Rademacher vectors), achieving O(d) computational complexity for billion-parameter networks. Parameters in high-curvature regions receive dampened updates to prevent overshooting (diagonal Newton-step behavior); flat regions receive larger relative updates. Thermodynamic framing defined as rigorous information-geometric metrics, not literal heat dissipation, ensuring patent eligibility under 35 U.S.C. § 101. Targets $100B+ AI infrastructure market. All rights reserved.

title: Automated grading of renal cell carcinoma using an efficient deep learning approach on histopathology images
abstract: In the healthcare industry, Renal Cell carcinoma (RCC) is the most common form of kidney cancer, and it is heterogeneous with intrinsic histopathological features. Moreover, grading RCC from the histopathology slides is essential for prognosis and determination of treatment strategy, but manual grading is labor intensive, time consuming and requires addressing inherent observer variability. Recently, Deep Learning (DL) approaches have shown significant advantages in medical image analysis, However, applying DL approaches to RCC grading still faces several challenge, which include small, annotated datasets and algorithms that can adequately represent intricate histopathological features. Besides, the proposed study provides datasets of digitalized histopathology scans of RCC slides, which are annotated by expert pathologists that are sufficient for training and testing models. Therefore, the proposed Dual Attention-Gated Dilated MobileNetV2 (DAG-DMobileNetV2) is employed for automated RCC grading. The model addresses these challenges by using dilated convolutions to increase the receptive field and generate a larger context without a reduction in resolution, hence allowing the model to extract both fine-grained and global features effectively. In addition, the dual attention mechanism, composed of channel and spatial attention mechanisms that enables the model to dynamically emphasize important areas and feature channels while suppressing irrelevant noise and concentrating on diagnostically important regions. Thus, the MobileNet backbone enables the model to operate efficiently, allowing for its suitability for deployment in real-time clinical settings. Hence, the contributions of the proposed model are the distinct attention modules coupled with dilated convolutions, allowing for accurate discrimination of the 4 different grades of RCC. Thus, the proposed DAG-DMobileNetV2 achieves improved classification performance, improved feature representation, and decreased computational complexity resulting in faster inference. Moreover, the attention mechanisms for DAG-DMobileNetV2 should automatically accommodate and adapt to variability in histopathological image quality.

title: Smart Alone, Blind Together: Why Accuracy Fails to CertifyTheory of Mind in Multi-Agent Teams
abstract: Coordinators that act on what they infer about teammates are usually certified by the accuracy of those inferences. We argue that accuracy is the wrong certificate, for two reasons. First, the accuracy needed to act depends on what a wrong action costs, so the bar belongs to the deployment, not the module. Second, a module's errors are rarely independent, and dependence has a sign: positively associated errors help where their damage overlaps and hurt where it compounds, so an accuracy threshold fails in a predictable direction, and once wrong beliefs interact and can do harm, no rule based on accuracy is right for every module. title: Task-evoked eye movements as candidate digital biomarkers of depression severity in adolescents and young adults
abstract: Objective digital measures of depression severity could complement conventional symptom assessments and facilitate more timely clinical evaluation. Here, we investigated whether task-evoked eye movements provide interpretable behavioral markers of depression severity in adolescents and young adults. In this single-center, cross-sectional study, 155 participants aged 14--20 years completed emotional-spatial free-viewing and memory-guided recall tasks and were stratified by 17-item Hamilton Depression Rating Scale scores. We examined 19 prespecified eye-movement features across six task-informed domains using covariate-adjusted ordinal-trend models. Greater depression severity was associated with lower gaze-allocation entropy (standardized $β=-0.599$), fewer inter-area switches ($β=-0.526$), longer first target-entry latency ($β=0.572$), and lower target dwell proportion ($β=-0.678$; all false-discovery-rate-adjusted $q<0.001$). Emotion-specific attentional-bias measures were not associated with severity, whereas associations involving fixation dispersion weakened after adjustment for anxiety symptoms. In a complementary machine-learning analysis incorporating 44 candidate eye-movement features and demographic covariates, a three-stage cascade classifier achieved the highest four-class stratification performance (accuracy, 0.665; macro-F1, 0.670; area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, 0.869), outperforming single-stage and two-stage approaches. Together, these findings identify altered visual exploration and memory-guided gaze control as candidate digital biomarkers of depression severity, rather than generalized negative attentional bias. These results support further prospective evaluation of task-evoked eye tracking as a complementary approach for timely severity assessment and clinical decision support.

title: Experimental Realization of a C-Shunt Flux-Qubit Coupler for Controlled-Z Gates between Transmons
abstract: Fast entangling gates and low-interaction idling require distinct operating conditions in superconducting quantum processors. We experimentally realize a transmon-C-shunt-transmon (TCT) device in which a flux-tunable, three-junction capacitively shunted flux-qubit coupler connects two transmon data qubits. The C-shunt coupler provides a flux-tunable, positively anharmonic spectrum for tailoring the interactions between the data qubits. Conditional Ramsey and swap measurements identify an idle region with near-zero residual ZZ interaction strength and suppressed transverse exchange. At this bias, simultaneous single-qubit interleaved randomized benchmarking yields X-gate fldelities above 99.7%, consistent with individual operation. A 45 ns nonadiabatic controlled-Z (CZ) gate achieves an interleaved randomized benchmarking fldelity estimate of 99.23(15)%. Numerical simulations identify coupler energy relaxation as an important limitation on CZ-gate fldelity and indicate that extending the coupler lifetime can improve gate performance. These results demonstrate the experimental feasibility of C-shunt flux-qubit couplers for combining low-interaction idling with fast entangling operations between transmon qubits.

title: Rarity Determines Minimax Rates of Semantic Entropy From Weak Pairwise Judgments With a Known Channel
abstract: The semantic entropy of a language model is the entropy of the meanings of its sampled answers. The meanings are never observed, and the entropy is estimated from the verdicts of a pairwise equivalence judge. Given the meanings of $n$ answers, a known channel declares each pair equivalent independently, with probability $q+Δ$ within a meaning and $q$ across meanings. At most $K$ meanings occur, and $q$ is bounded away from $0$ and $1$. For a weak judge, with $nΔ^2\to0$, the global minimax rate is set by distributions near a vertex of the simplex and overstates the difficulty elsewhere. We show that the difficulty is set by how many meanings can be rare. Over distributions with at most $s$ meanings below a fixed probability $τ<1/(K-s)$, the minimax squared risk is of order $N^{-1/s}$ for $s\ge2$, $N^{-1}\log^2(e+N)$ for $s=1$ and $N^{-1}$ for $s=0$, capped at one, where $N=n^KΔ^{2K-2}$. The matching lower bounds hold on every fixed polynomial window $nΔ^2\le n^{-κ}$. One estimator attains these rates without knowing $s$ or $τ$: it averages products of centered verdicts along all spanning trees of every $k$-set of answers, projects the resulting power sums onto the valid moment set and inverts them. The case $s=K-1$ gives the global rate $N^{-1/(K-1)}$ and the consistency threshold: with $Δ=n^{-γ}$ the entropy is uniformly consistently estimable exactly when $γ<K/(2K-2)$. On polynomial windows, the same estimator attains the sharp local minimax constant on shrinking neighborhoods of interior points with distinct probabilities. Restricting the average to stars multiplies the constant by $K^{K-3}$.

title: Merit: Making every modality earn its contribution in multimodal attention decoding
abstract: More than 1.5 billion people have hearing loss. When several people talk at once, hearing aids amplify every voice alike. Auditory attention decoding (AAD) aims to solve this by reading a listener's brain signals to find the attended talker, letting the device amplify only them. A real device will not see the brain alone; smart glasses and earbuds also track eyes, head, and scene. These behavioral signals help, as people often look at who they listen to. However, they show where a listener looks, not whom they hear. A decoder relying heavily on them fails when a listener cannot move their head or listens without looking - exactly when a brain-based device is needed. A multimodal decoder must use these signals without letting them replace the electroencephalogram (EEG). Accuracy alone cannot show whether it does. We present MERIT, a decoder and evaluation method asking: how much accuracy does each input earn? MERIT shuffles each input stream across test examples, measures the accuracy drop, and splits the result across streams using Shapley values. It also blocks two shortcuts: candidate audio is checked before training so it cannot reveal the answer, and the scoring function cannot beat chance if it ignores the brain. On a public dataset with EEG, eye tracking, head motion, and scene video, MERIT improves on the published benchmark, reaching 0.82 four-way accuracy within listeners and 0.74 on unseen listeners (chance is 0.25). The measurement reveals what accuracy hides: adding behavioral streams raises overall accuracy but almost halves the brain's share of it. On two other datasets, the same tests find a label imbalance in a widely used benchmark and flag results that accuracy alone would report as brain decoding.

title: MONTE CARLO TREE SEARCH: A REVIEW OF DRAWBACKS, ADVANTAGES AND LIMITATIONS IN COMPLEX MULTIPLAYER GAMES
abstract: O MCTS ganhou destaque após sucessos em Go, Xadrez e Shogi, mas a maioria dos estudos concentra-se em jogos de dois jogadores com informação perfeita. Este artigo analisa o MCTS em jogos digitais e de tabuleiro multijogador, frequentemente caracterizados por informação imperfeita. Com base em 18 artigos selecionados entre 22 recuperados nas bases IEEE Xplore, HAL Science Ouverte e Google Scholar (2013–2025), o estudo identifica três limitações estruturais recorrentes: platôs computacionais, pontos cegos no raciocínio tático e trade-offs na modelagem de oponentes. Além disso, mostra que a informação imperfeita e as restrições de tempo real intensificam essas limitações. O artigo também reúne estratégias de mitigação, como ajuste via NTBEA, playouts baseados em conhecimento especializado e Information Set MCTS, além de apontar cinco lacunas de pesquisa em ambientes pouco explorados, incluindo jogos digitais em tempo real, jogos de cartas cooperativos e jogos de tabuleiro modernos.

title: The Impact of Data Quality on Machine Learning Model Performance
abstract: This research examines the impact of data quality on the performance of machine learning classification models. The study focuses on three common data-quality factors: missing data, feature selection, and label noise. Three machine learning models (Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, and Random Forest) are evaluated on the Titanic dataset using Accuracy and F1-score. A series of experiments modifies the quality and structure of the dataset while keeping the general modeling approach consistent. The results show that different types of data-quality problems affect models to different degrees: label noise can cause a substantial decrease in predictive performance, while the effects of missing data and feature selection depend on the model and experimental conditions. The study also compares the sensitivity of the algorithms to data-quality problems and evaluates whether the research hypothesis is supported by the results. Independent research project. Implemented in Python using pandas, NumPy, matplotlib, and scikit-learn.

title: TABIIY VA SUN'IY YARATILGAN MATNLARNI FARQLASHDA LINGVISTIK-STATISTIK BELGILAR TAHLILI
abstract: Maqolada tabiiy matnlar hamda sinonimlash va Markov zanjirlari yordamida yaratilgan sun'iy matnlarni farqlash masalasi lingvistik-statistik belgilar nuqtayi nazaridan ko'rib chiqiladi. Manbada keltirilgan 21 ta miqdoriy xususiyat, jumladan so'z uzunligi, tinish belgilari, xizmat so'zlari, gap tuzilishi, grammatik xatolar va semantik yadro ko'rsatkichlari qiyosiy tahlil qilinadi. Natijalar ayrim belgilar sun'iy matn sinflarini ajratishda foydali bo'lishini, biroq bitta belgi asosida ishonchli xulosa chiqarish yetarli emasligini ko'rsatadi. Shu sababli belgilar majmuasidan foydalanish va matnning turli lingvistik darajalarini birgalikda baholash zarurligi asoslanadi.

title: TITLE Conceptual Worldbuilding & Generative Realities at the Limit DESCRIPTION Conceptual Worldbuilding & Generative Realities at the Limit develops a falsifiable research architecture for turning concepts into interactive digital worlds, social simulations, digital twins, and institutional prototypes without confusing internal coherence with external reality. The book is organized around a core tri-coupling: Conceptual Rules × Executable Worlds × Reality Feedback. Its central candidate relation is WorldValidity = RuleCoherence × TaskReplay × ExternalTransfer, with a strict condition: ExternalTransfer remains UNKNOWN until independently tested. Immersion, elegance, agent fluency, and repeated success inside a simulator are treated as insufficient evidence of causal validity in the physical or institutional world. The volume contains a thirty-formula mathematical prelude, eighty-two chapters in a single-section-per-page architecture, two hundred Research Gates, thirty-three Phoenix Answer Embryos, and 233 Easter-Egg Equations. It integrates state-space models, conservation laws, stochastic processes, causal inference, robust control, information theory, game theory, network dynamics, transfer geometry, digital-twin validation, rights constraints, resource ledgers, participatory governance, data portability, shutdown, and responsible world retirement. Five research layers structure the work: declaring boundaries and state transitions; compiling concepts into versioned rules; testing counterfactuals, scarcity, rights, and extreme conditions; cross-validating simulations with real-world data; and designing world branching, refusal, exit, shutdown, and succession. The result is a world-rule package, a digital-prototype methodology, and a transfer-failure map for researchers, designers, policymakers, AI system builders, and future civilizational studies. This is a research architecture rather than a claim that generated worlds are newly created physical universes. Book-defined equations are candidate models and indicators, not validated natural laws. Every major claim is paired with an applicability domain, measurement path, competing explanation, falsification boundary, and successor revision route. Author: Feng Cheng-En (pen name: 33)

title: Aspect–Sentiment Triplet Extraction in Low-Resource Odia Language Using a Tri-Channel GCN
abstract: With the proliferation of digital platforms and smartphones, users increasingly express opinions in their native languages through online reviews. However, fine-grained sentiment analysis for such low-resource languages remains underexplored, as most Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis (ABSA) methods target resource-rich languages such as English. To address this gap, we present Odia-TriGCN, a hybrid framework for Aspect Sentiment Triplet Extraction in the low-resource Odia language. title: Focus, Align, and Diffuse: Time-Series-Aware Keyframe Diffusion for Cardiac Dynamic Synthesis from Sparse Observations
abstract: Dense cardiac dynamics are essential for assessing cardiac function, yet in practice clinicians often observe only extremely sparse measurements. However, recovering full dynamics from such sparsity is a highly ill-posed problem due to the lack of temporal cues. While auxiliary time-series signals like ECG provide physiological guidance, effectively exploiting them is challenging due to the cross-modal representation gap and phase misalignment. In this work, we present CardioFAD, a Focus--Align--Diffuse paradigm that reformulates sparse cardiac dynamic synthesis as a recoverability--alignability anchor discovery problem. Our core insight is that resolving extreme temporal ambiguity requires a compact set of anchor states that are both sufficient to recover the visual trajectory and reliable for ECG--visual alignment. We therefore learn motion-salient keyframes under two complementary principles: trajectory sufficiency, which preserves trajectory-critical intra-modal motion content, and anchor alignment, which promotes consistent inter-modal correspondence at these anchors. We implement the Focus and Align modules optimized by the two aspects. Diffuse then performs two-stage generation by first synthesizing keyframes and subsequently interpolating the remaining frames. Extensive experiments on cardiac MRI and echocardiography videos demonstrate superior visual quality, temporal coherence, and improved functional consistency under the extreme one-shot regime.

title: Operator Surrogates
abstract: This chapter provides a mathematical introduction to operator surrogates, which are finite-parametric maps approximating complex (typically nonlinear) operators between infinite-dimensional (function) spaces. A typical approach to constructing operator surrogates is the encoder-approximator-decoder paradigm, whereby infinite-dimensional inputs are mapped to a finite-dimensional latent space, processed, and then mapped back to the infinite-dimensional output space. We discuss various methods for creating efficient representation systems, including stable linear frameworks like Banach frames and data-driven techniques such as Principal Component Analysis (PCA), Active Subspaces, and nonlinear autoencoders. Subsequently, we survey key surrogate architectures, contrasting spectral methods, based on polynomial chaos expansions and related technologies, with more recent neural network approaches. We further discuss architectures that do not rely on representation systems, such as Fourier Neural Operators and transformers. We elaborate on their relationship and how they relate to other neural network operator surrogates, particularly those obtained by so-called "algorithm-unrolling". Additionally, we provide an introduction to the theoretical analysis of approximation and generalization errors. We explain how underlying low-dimensional structures, provided for example by holomorphy, are essential to overcome the so-called "curse of dimensionality": this refers to the fact that the complexity of numerical algorithms tends to increase exponentially in the problem dimensionality. We present convergence rate bounds for holomorphic operators that depend on the number of trainable parameters and the regularity of the input and output data. Throughout, we prioritize intuition over detailed technical proofs and provide precise pointers to the literature for detailed arguments.
